definition_zh: 冒险事业；风险投资；动词：敢于去、冒险做；大胆提出
definition_en: a risky or daring enterprise, or to go somewhere or say something despite the danger
core_image: 一条小船离开熟悉的岸边，驶向看不清的雾里
scene: 天还没亮，几条渔船却已经解开缆绳驶向外海。Few boats ventured out in such heavy fog.
sceneCN: 这里 venture 是「冒险前往」（第 3 个义项：冒着风险去某处）；句意为浓雾之中很少有船敢出海。小船离岸驶入雾里，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：冒险事业；风险投资；投机
动词：冒险前往；敢于做；大胆提出

collocations.zh: 冒昧地做某事；斗胆做某事

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -some 构成，义为「好冒险的；敢于尝试的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「冒险者；合资经营参与者」
同源自拉丁语 advenire 的词，义为「冒险；奇遇」
与 adventure 同源，义为「爱冒险的」

senses.title: A daring enterprise
senses.titleCN: 冒险事业：有风险的事业
senses.definition: a new business activity or project that involves risk of loss
senses.definitionCN: 一项承担亏损风险的新生意或新项目
senses.example: Opening a shop in a quiet town was a bold venture.
senses.exampleCN: 在冷清的小镇开店是一次大胆的冒险事业。
senses.why: Latin venire means to come, and what is ventured is an outcome that has not yet come; you commit before you know it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 venire 意为「来」，venture 的结果尚未到来；你在知道结果之前就已经下了注。

senses.title: Money put at risk
senses.titleCN: 风险投资：押上去的资本
senses.definition: money or capital invested in a risky project in the hope of large profit
senses.definitionCN: 投入有风险项目、期望高额回报的资金
senses.example: The firm put its first venture capital into a small software team.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司把第一笔风险投资投给了一个小型软件团队。
senses.why: The abstract enterprise becomes a sum of money: the risk is now measurable in cash.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的冒险事业化为具体的金额：风险此时可以用钱来衡量。

senses.title: To dare to go
senses.titleCN: 冒险前往：敢去某个地方
senses.definition: to go somewhere that may be dangerous or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 敢于前往可能危险或令人不快的地方
senses.example: No one ventured into the flooded tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人冒险进入那条被淹的隧道。
senses.why: The verb keeps the picture of leaving safe ground: the body moves first, the guarantee comes later or never.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了离开安全地面这一画面：身体先动，保障之后才来，也许永远不来。

senses.title: To dare to say
senses.titleCN: 斗胆说：敢于提出意见
senses.definition: to say or suggest something that may be unwelcome or may be wrong
senses.definitionCN: 敢于说出可能不受欢迎或可能出错的话
senses.example: May I venture a different explanation?
senses.exampleCN: 我可以冒昧地提一个不同的解释吗？
senses.why: Speaking up is also a step into the open; the speaker risks being wrong in front of others.
senses.whyCN: 开口说话同样是走进开阔处；说话人要冒着在众人面前出错的风险。

senses.title: To try something new
senses.titleCN: 敢于尝试：试着做没做过的事
senses.definition: to attempt something new or difficult despite the chance of failure
senses.definitionCN: 尽管可能失败，仍尝试新事物或难做的事
senses.example: She ventured a smile at the stranger across the aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 她朝过道上那位陌生人试着笑了一下。
senses.why: The core image is small here but unchanged: a step taken without knowing how it will be received.
senses.whyCN: 这里的意象虽小却没有改变：在不知道会被如何接受的情况下迈出一步。

intro.en: Venture is a clipped form of adventure, which came from Latin through Old French; the family all turns on the verb 'to come'.
intro.cn: venture 是 adventure 的截短形式，后者经由古法语来自拉丁语；整个词族都围绕「来」这个动词。

items.en: The verb venire meant 'to come'; its future participle venturus described what is going to come.
items.cn: 动词 venire 意为「来」，其将来分词 venturus 指「将要到来的事」。

items.en: Medieval Latin adventura meant 'things about to happen', used for what fate would bring.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 adventura 意为「将要发生的事」，用来指命运会带来什么。

items.en: Old French aventure carried the sense of chance, hazard and a risky undertaking.
items.cn: 古法语 aventure 带有「机遇、风险、冒险之举」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed aventure in the thirteenth century; the shorter venture split off as a separate word.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 aventure；较短的形式 venture 后来独立成一个词。

items.en: Commerce made venture a practical word: joint venture and venture capital name enterprises with money at risk.
items.cn: 商业让 venture 变成务实之词：joint venture 与 venture capital 都指押着钱的经营行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same 'come' family; the near-meaning group gathers nouns and verbs for risk-taking.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「来」词根的一族词；近义组收表示冒险的名词与动词。

entries.definition: An exciting or dangerous experience; the longer form from which venture was cut.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冒险、奇遇」，是 venture 由之截短的较长形式。

entries.definition: Something that happens; literally that which comes out.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件」，字面意思就是「出来的事」。

entries.definition: To stop something from coming about; pre- plus venire.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「阻止」，由 pre- 加 venire「来」构成。

entries.definition: To devise something new; literally to come upon an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发明」，字面上是「碰上、遇见」一个想法。

entries.definition: The chance of loss itself; venture is the undertaking that carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风险」，指损失的可能性本身；venture 是承担风险的那件事。

entries.definition: To bet on an uncertain result; more openly about chance and money.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「赌博、押注」，更直接地指机会与金钱。

entries.definition: A task or project one commits to, without the stress on danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承担的事业、任务」，不特别强调危险。

entries.definition: To be bold enough to do something frightening; the nerve rather than the project.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「敢于」，强调胆量而非事业本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb venire and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语动词 venire，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: venture is adventure without the ad: the same risky trip, said shorter.
normal.cn: venture 就是去掉 ad 的 adventure：同一趟冒险，说得更短。

normal.en: Joint venture is a business born of two partners, both risking money.
normal.cn: joint venture 是两家合作生出的生意，双方都押了钱。

normal.en: Venture capital names money that dares to fund an unproven idea.
normal.cn: venture capital 指敢去资助尚未验证的想法的钱。

normal.en: To venture out is to leave the house when the weather warns against it.
normal.cn: venture out 就是在天气示警时仍走出家门。

normal.en: Nothing ventured, nothing gained: no risk taken means no gain made.
normal.cn: 不入虎穴焉得虎子：不承担风险就得不到收获。

abstract.en: See the word as a boat leaving the harbour: the shore is the known, the fog is the coming, and the boat moves before it can see.
abstract.cn: 把这个词想成一条离港的小船：岸是已知，雾是将要到来的事，而船在看清之前就已经出发。

abstract.en: Everything in the word happens before the result arrives: venture is always on the side of the untested.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的事都发生在结果到来之前：venture 永远站在未经检验的一边。

abstract.en: The same move can be a business, a journey or a sentence; all three are steps into the open.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作可以是一桩生意、一段路程或一句话；三者都是走进开阔处的一步。

examples.en: They launched a small venture selling solar lamps to remote villages.
examples.cn: 他们创办了一家小型企业，向偏远村庄销售太阳能灯。

examples.en: Nobody ventured outside until the storm had passed.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过去之前，没有人敢出门。

examples.en: The two firms formed a joint venture to build the bridge.
examples.cn: 这两家公司组建合资企业来修建这座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「万一扯」——船万一被扯离岸边，就只能往前闯：冒险

root: 为 adventure 的截短形式，源自拉丁语 venire「来」的将来分词 venturus「将要来临的」，经中世纪拉丁语 adventura 与古法语 aventure 进入英语；同族词有 event、prevent、invent。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of venture run from the abstract enterprise to the capital behind it, then to the small daily daring of going, saying and trying.
sensesIntro.cn: venture 的五个义项从抽象的冒险事业出发，到其背后的资本，再到出门、开口、试探这些日常里的小胆量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boat leaves the shore and steers into fog before it can see the far side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条船离开岸边，在看清对岸之前就驶进雾里。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the risky project and the capital that funds it.
branches.cn: 资本线：冒险的项目以及资助它的资金。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the feet move into a place that may harm them.
branches.cn: 身体线：双脚走进可能有害的地方。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: the mouth risks a remark that may be wrong.
branches.cn: 声音线：嘴巴冒着出错的风险说出看法。

branches.en: GESTURE LINE: the smallest step, a smile offered to a stranger.
branches.cn: 姿态线：最小的一步，比如向陌生人递出的微笑。

branches.en: CONTRAST: adventure is the same word with more colour, venture the cooler business face.
branches.cn: 对照线：adventure 更带色彩，venture 则是更冷静的商业面孔。

intro.en: Venture inherits a Latin verb stem plus English endings; its parts are transparent once the family is known.
intro.cn: venture 继承了拉丁语动词词干并接英语词尾；认识这个词族之后，各部分都很清楚。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is verifiable: venire, to come, with its participle venturus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：venire「来」及其分词 venturus。

items.example: It carries the core of the word.
It turns the verb stem into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词词干变成名词。

definition_zh: 核实；证实；查证；验证（身份、数据、真伪）
definition_en: to check or prove that something is true, accurate or genuine
core_image: 一只手把证据和账本逐条核对，最后在末尾打上勾
scene: 门卫拦下访客，让他出示证件，又对着名单一个字母一个字母地核对。The guard verified her name against the list before opening the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 verify 是「核实、查证」（第 1 个义项：检查某事是否真实准确）；句意为门卫开门前对照名单核实了她的名字。逐条核对再打勾的动作，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：核实、查证；证实；验证

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ication 构成，义为「核实；验证」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可核实的；可验证的」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「已核实的；经验证的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「核实者；校验器」

senses.title: To check the facts
senses.titleCN: 核实：检查事实是否正确
senses.definition: to check that information is true or accurate
senses.definitionCN: 检查信息是否真实、准确
senses.example: Please verify the figures before the report goes out.
senses.exampleCN: 报告发布之前请核实这些数字。
senses.why: Latin verus means true and facere means to make; to verify is to make a thing true in the sense of proving it so.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 verus 意为「真」，facere 意为「做」；verify 就是通过证明来把一件事确立为真。

senses.title: To confirm with evidence
senses.titleCN: 证实：拿出证据来确认
senses.definition: to establish the truth of something by presenting evidence
senses.definitionCN: 通过出示证据来确立某事的真实性
senses.example: Two independent witnesses verified his account.
senses.exampleCN: 两名独立证人证实了他的说法。
senses.why: Checking becomes proving when evidence is laid beside the claim, as one pan of a balance beside the other.
senses.whyCN: 当证据被摆在说法一旁，如同天平两边相对，核对就变成了证实。

senses.title: To confirm identity
senses.titleCN: 核验身份：确认是不是本人
senses.definition: to establish that a person or document is genuine, as with a passport or password
senses.definitionCN: 确认某个人或证件真实无误，如查验护照或密码
senses.example: Banks must verify the identity of every new customer.
senses.exampleCN: 银行必须核验每一位新客户的身份。
senses.why: A person can be 'true' too: the same test applies to who someone is, not only to what a claim says.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以是「真的」：同一套检验既用于一句话是否属实，也用于一个人是谁。

senses.title: To test a system or figure
senses.titleCN: 验证：检验数据或系统是否成立
senses.definition: to test a result, calculation or system to show that it works as claimed
senses.definitionCN: 检验结果、计算或系统是否如所称那样运行
senses.example: The engineers verified the bridge design with a computer model.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用计算机模型验证了桥梁设计。
senses.why: Here the truth under test is a working thing, and the test produces the proof.
senses.whyCN: 此时受检验的「真」是一件能运转的东西，而检验本身就产出了证明。

senses.title: As in verified accounts
senses.titleCN: 见于「已认证」之类说法
senses.definition: used adjectivally in phrases such as a verified account, meaning officially confirmed
senses.definitionCN: 以形容词形式用于 verified account「已认证账号」等说法，意为经官方确认的
senses.example: Her verified account carries a small blue badge.
senses.exampleCN: 她的已认证账号上带着一个小小的蓝色标记。
senses.why: The act becomes a state: once the check is done, the mark stays on the thing.
senses.whyCN: 动作变成了状态：核对一旦完成，标记就留在那件东西上。

intro.en: Verify joins two Latin words, verus 'true' and facere 'to make', and the pair travelled through French into English.
intro.cn: verify 由两个拉丁词合成：verus「真」与 facere「做」，这一组合经法语进入英语。

items.en: The adjective verus meant 'true, real, genuine', and it also gave veritas 'truth'.
items.cn: 形容词 verus 意为「真的、真实的」，它还生出 veritas「真理」。

items.en: The verb facere meant 'to make, do', the source of dozens of English -fy verbs.
items.cn: 动词 facere 意为「做、造」，是英语许多以 -fy 结尾动词的来源。

items.en: Verificare meant 'to make true, prove to be true'; the medieval form is documented, though its first use is uncertain.
items.cn: verificare 意为「使成真、证明为真」；这一中世纪形式有文献可查，但首见年代不确定。

items.en: Old French verifier carried the sense of proving or establishing a thing as true.
items.cn: 古法语 verifier 带有「证明或确立某事物为真」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed verify in the fourteenth century, first in legal and scholarly contexts.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 verify，最初多用于法律与学术语境。

items.en: Computing gave the word a technical life: to verify data, a signature or an account.
items.cn: 计算机领域赋予这个词技术生命：验证数据、签名或账号。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other Latin -ficare verbs; the near-meaning group gathers ways of checking and confirming.
note.cn: 形近组收其他拉丁语 -ficare 动词；近义组收各种核对与确认的说法。

entries.definition: To make something clear; clarus 'clear' plus facere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「澄清」，由 clarus「清楚」加 facere 构成。

entries.definition: To confirm officially in writing; certus 'sure' plus facere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证明、颁发证书」，由 certus「确定」加 facere 构成。

entries.definition: To recognise or establish who or what something is.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「识别、确认身份」。

entries.definition: The noun of checking that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「核实、验证」。

entries.definition: To state that something is certainly true, often after being asked.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「确认」，常在被询问之后表示某事确实如此。

entries.definition: To look at something quickly to see whether it is right; the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「检查」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To prove something is valid or acceptable, especially by official test.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使生效、验证有效」，多指经过正式检验。

entries.definition: To support a claim with evidence; formal and heavy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证实、用证据支持」，语气正式而厚重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real Latin parts, verus and facere, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语两部件 verus 与 facere，以及这个词出现的短语。

normal.en: veri- is true and -fy is to make: verify is to make true by proof.
normal.cn: veri- 是真，-fy 是做：verify 就是靠证明把事做真。

normal.en: Verify comes before you trust; confirm often comes when someone asks.
normal.cn: verify 发生在你相信之前；confirm 多发生在有人问起时。

normal.en: Verification is the noun, verifiable the adjective: check, then the checkable quality.
normal.cn: verification 是名词，verifiable 是形容词：先核对，再谈可核对的性质。

normal.en: A verified account has passed the check and keeps the badge.
normal.cn: 已认证账号通过了核对，于是保留那个标记。

normal.en: Computers verify a password in milliseconds; a witness may take years.
normal.cn: 计算机毫秒之间校验密码，而一个证人可能要用好几年。

abstract.en: Picture two columns on a page: the claim on the left, the evidence on the right, and a tick when they line up.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上两栏：左边是说法，右边是证据，两者对齐时打一个勾。

abstract.en: The word is built to make truth, not to find it: the act of proving is what creates the certainty.
abstract.cn: 这个词生来是要「造出」真，而不是「发现」真：证明这一动作本身造出了确定。

abstract.en: The same tick works for facts, for identity and for a design that must hold a bridge.
abstract.cn: 同一个勾适用于事实、身份，以及必须撑住一座桥的设计。

examples.en: Journalists must verify a story before publishing it.
examples.cn: 记者在发表报道之前必须核实。

examples.en: The software verifies your password each time you log in.
examples.cn: 每次登录时，软件都会校验你的密码。

examples.en: Officials could not verify the number of people in the camp.
examples.cn: 官员无法核实营地中的人数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「verify 为瑞发」——为瑞（veri）发一张证明，核料必须是真的：核实

root: 由拉丁语 verus「真的」与 facere「做、造」组合而成，中世纪拉丁语 verificare「证明为真」，经古法语 verifier 进入英语；同族词有 verity、verdict、clarify、certify。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of verify move from checking a fact, to proving it with evidence, to testing a person, a system, and finally the lasting mark of a passed check.
sensesIntro.cn: verify 的五个义项从核对事实，到用证据证实，再到检验一个人、一套系统，最后落在通过核验后留下的持久标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two columns on a page, claim and evidence, with a tick where they meet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页纸上的两栏，说法与证据，在二者吻合处打一个勾。

branches.en: CHECK LINE: the eye runs down the list comparing each item.
branches.cn: 核对线：目光沿清单逐项比对。

branches.en: PROOF LINE: evidence is set beside the claim until the balance is level.
branches.cn: 证明线：把证据摆在说法旁边，直到天平持平。

branches.en: TEST LINE: a person or a system is put through the same test.
branches.cn: 检验线：人和系统都要经过同一套检验。

branches.en: MARK LINE: the finished check leaves a badge behind.
branches.cn: 标记线：核验完成后留下一个标记。

branches.en: CONTRAST: check looks, verify proves, confirm answers.
branches.cn: 对照线：check 是看，verify 是证明，confirm 是应声作答。

intro.en: Verify is a Latin compound: a true-root plus a make-root, closed by English endings.
intro.cn: verify 是拉丁语复合词：一个「真」词根加一个「做」词根，再以英语词尾收束。

latinIntro.en: Both Latin halves are documented: verus and facere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的两半都有文献可查：verus 与 facere。

items.example: It carries the idea of truth.

items.exampleCN: 它连接 verus 与 facere。
它构成 clarify 与 certify。

definition_zh: 版本；说法、描述；（软件、文件的）修订本；改编本
definition_en: a particular form of something that differs from other forms of it, such as a copy, an account, or an edition
core_image: 同一份稿子被改了又改，桌上摊着好几份，每一份都略有不同
scene: 编辑把同一篇文章的三个版本并排打开，逐段比较。The final version was shorter than the first one by two pages.
sceneCN: 这里 version 是「版本」（第 1 个义项：与同一事物的其他形式不同的某个形态）；句意为最终版本比第一版短了两页。几份稿子并排放在桌上，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：版本；说法；改编本；译文

collocations.phrase: a film version of the novel

derivatives.zh: 加形容词后缀构成，义为「与版本有关的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「版本管理、版本化」
同一拉丁词根 vert-「转」构成，义为「多才多艺的；多用途的」
同一词根构成，义为「转换；改变信仰」

senses.title: One form among many
senses.titleCN: 版本：众多形态中的一种
senses.definition: a particular form of something, in which it differs from other forms of the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的一种特定形态，与其他形态有所差别
senses.example: The paper published a longer version of the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸刊登了那次访谈的较长版本。
senses.why: Latin vertere means to turn; a version is the same matter turned a little differently.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vertere 意为「转」；version 就是同一件事被稍稍转了个角度。

senses.title: One person's account
senses.titleCN: 说法：某人对事情的一种讲法
senses.definition: one person's account of an event, especially when others may tell it differently
senses.definitionCN: 某人对一件事的讲述，尤指他人可能有不同讲法时
senses.example: The two witnesses gave very different versions of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 两名证人对事故的说法大相径庭。
senses.why: An account is also a turning: the same event passes through one perspective and comes out shaped by it.
senses.whyCN: 讲述同样是一种转动：同一件事经过一个人的视角，出来时已被这个视角塑形。

senses.title: An edition or revision
senses.titleCN: 修订本：经过修改的一版
senses.definition: a revised or updated edition of a text, file or product
senses.definitionCN: 文本、文件或产品经过修改更新的一个版本
senses.example: This is the third version of the manual, and it is much clearer.
senses.exampleCN: 这是手册的第三版，清楚多了。
senses.why: Each revision turns the draft once more, and the newest turn is what users install.
senses.whyCN: 每一次修订都把稿子再转一次，最新的那一转就是用户安装的那个。

senses.title: An adaptation
senses.titleCN: 改编本：由原作改成的形式
senses.definition: a form of a work that has been adapted for another medium or audience
senses.definitionCN: 为另一种媒介或受众改编而成的作品形式
senses.example: The film version leaves out the youngest brother entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 电影改编版把最小的弟弟整个删掉了。
senses.why: Moving a story to the screen is a literal turning: the same characters now seen from a new side.
senses.whyCN: 把故事搬上银幕是一种字面意义上的转动：同一些人物从新的方向被看见。

senses.title: A specific release of software
senses.titleCN: 软件的一个具体发行版
senses.definition: a numbered release of a program or document, used to track changes over time
senses.definitionCN: 带编号的程序或文档发行版本，用于追踪变化
senses.example: Please update to version 4.2 before sending the file.
senses.exampleCN: 发送文件之前请更新到 4.2 版。
senses.why: In modern use the turning is numbered: each fix produces one more version on the record.
senses.whyCN: 在现代用法里，这种转动被编了号：每修一处，记录上就多一个版本。

intro.en: Version comes from the Latin verb 'to turn', and the whole family follows that image of turning.
intro.cn: version 源自拉丁语表示「转」的动词，整个词族都沿着这一转动的意象展开。

items.en: The verb vertere meant 'to turn, turn around, change'; it lies behind convert, revert and reverse.
items.cn: 动词 vertere 意为「转、回转、改变」，它是 convert、revert、reverse 背后的词。

items.en: Versio meant 'a turning, a change, a translation'; the noun names the act of turning something.
items.cn: versio 意为「转动、改变、翻译」，这一名词指把某物转一次这件事。

items.en: Old French borrowed the word for a translation or rendering of a text.
items.cn: 古法语借入这个词，指文本的翻译或转写。

items.en: English adopted version first for translations, then for any form differing from another.
items.cn: 英语最初用 version 指译本，后来泛指与其他形式有别的任一形态。

items.en: Publishing, then computing, turned it into a counting word: first version, final version, version number.
items.cn: 出版业再到计算机业把它变成计数词：第一版、最终版、版本号。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin turn-root; the near-meaning group gathers words for forms and accounts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「转」词根构成的词；近义组收表示形态与说法的词。

entries.definition: The act of turning something into another form or use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「转换、转变」，指把某物变成另一形态或用途。

entries.definition: To turn the other way round; the opposite direction of the same turn.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「颠倒、反转」，是同一转动的相反方向。

entries.definition: Turned apart, hence different; a family voice of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，本义为「转向不同方向」。

entries.definition: Able to turn to many uses or skills.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多才多艺的、多用途的」，即能转向许多用途。

entries.definition: One printing or published form of a text, usually revised.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版次」，指文本的一次印行，通常经过修订。

entries.definition: A report or description of what happened; the everyday word for sense 02.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「叙述、说法」，是义项 02 的日常词。

entries.definition: A form that differs slightly, often in spelling or wording.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变体」，指略有差别的形式，多指拼写或措辞。

entries.definition: A performance or translation of a work, stressing the performer's version.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演绎、译文」，强调表演者或译者的处理。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb vertere and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语动词 vertere，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: version shares its root with turn: each version is the same thing turned again.
normal.cn: version 与 turn 同根：每个版本都是同一件东西又转过一次。

normal.en: Different witnesses, different versions: the same event turned through different eyes.
normal.cn: 不同的证人给出不同的说法：同一件事经过不同的眼睛转动一次。

normal.en: Software asks for a version number; a novel asks for a film version.
normal.cn: 软件要的是版本号；小说要的是电影改编版。

normal.en: The original version stays the reference while later versions move away from it.
normal.cn: 原版始终是参照，后来的版本则离它越来越远。

normal.en: Ver- inside version echoes vertere, the turning verb of Latin.
normal.cn: version 里的 ver- 呼应 vertere，即拉丁语那个「转」的动词。

abstract.en: Picture one sheet of paper on a turntable: each small rotation shows a slightly different face, and each face is a version.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸放在转盘上：每一次微转都露出略不同的正面，每一面都是一个版本。

abstract.en: A version is never the thing itself, only a way of seeing it, which is why accounts can disagree.
abstract.cn: 版本从来不是事物本身，只是一种看它的方式，所以各种说法可以彼此矛盾。

abstract.en: The word travels from clay tablets to code without changing its logic: turn, compare, number.
abstract.cn: 这个词从泥板一路走到代码，逻辑却没变：转动、比较、编号。

examples.en: This is an older version of the map, without the new road.
examples.cn: 这是这幅地图的旧版本，上面还没有那条新路。

examples.en: Each witness told a slightly different version of the night.
examples.cn: 每个证人对那一夜的讲述都略有不同。

examples.en: The app will not open until you install the latest version.
examples.cn: 不安装最新版本，这个应用就打不开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我（ver）想（sion）」——同一个故事，我想的说法和别人不一样：版本

root: 源自拉丁语 versio「转动、翻译」，来自动词 vertere「转」；经古法语进入英语；同族词有 convert、reverse、diverse、versatile。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of version all rest on one turning: the same matter presented in another form, as an account, an edition, an adaptation, or a numbered release.
sensesIntro.cn: version 的五个义项都建立在一次转之上：同一件事以另一种形态出现，或是说法、或是修订本、或是改编、或是编号发行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sheets of one article side by side on a desk, each slightly changed.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一篇文章的几份稿子并排在桌上，每份都略有变化。

branches.en: FORM LINE: the noun names any one form of many.
branches.cn: 形态线：名词指众多形态中的任意一种。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: an account is the event turned through one person.
branches.cn: 说法线：说法就是事件经过某个人转动后的样子。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: editions and software releases are numbered turns.
branches.cn: 计数线：版本与软件发行都是被编号的一次转动。

branches.en: MEDIUM LINE: the story turns from page to screen.
branches.cn: 媒介线：故事从纸面转到银幕。

branches.en: CONTRAST: the original is the point from which every version departs.
branches.cn: 对照线：原版是所有版本由之离开的那个点。

intro.en: Version is a Latin noun stem with an English noun ending; the turning root stays visible inside it.
intro.cn: version 是拉丁语名词词干加英语名词词尾，其中的「转」词根仍清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vertere, with the noun versio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：动词 vertere 及其名词 versio。

items.example: It forms version from the stem.

definition_zh: 垂直的；竖的；纵向的；名词：垂直线、垂直方向
definition_en: going straight up and down, at a right angle to the flat ground or to a horizontal line
core_image: 一根铅垂线从屋檐垂下，线与地面严格成直角
scene: 木匠把线坠挂在刚起的墙边，眯眼一看，线垂得笔直。The wall was not vertical, and the whole frame had to be reset.
sceneCN: 这里 vertical 是「垂直的」（第 1 个义项：与地面成直角、竖直向上向下）；句意为墙不垂直，整个框架都得重做。沿墙面垂下的铅垂线，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：垂直的；竖式的；纵向的
名词：垂直线；垂直面

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「垂直地；竖直地」
加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「垂直性；竖直程度」
同源自拉丁语 vertex「顶点」，义为「顶点；最高点」
加动词后缀构成，义为「使垂直；使纵向化」

senses.title: Straight up and down
senses.titleCN: 垂直的：竖直上下
senses.definition: going straight up and down, at a right angle to the horizontal
senses.definitionCN: 笔直向上向下，与水平面成直角
senses.example: A vertical line joins the top of the page to the bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 一条垂直线把页面顶部和底部连起来。
senses.why: Latin vertex means the top or the turning point at the crown; the vertical is the direction that points to the crown.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vertex 指头顶的顶点或转点；vertical 就是指向头顶的那个方向。

senses.title: Of an axis or graph
senses.titleCN: 纵轴的：图表中上下方向
senses.definition: relating to the axis that runs up and down on a graph
senses.definitionCN: 指图表中上下延伸的那一条轴
senses.example: Temperature is shown on the vertical axis of the chart.
senses.exampleCN: 图表的纵轴表示温度。
senses.why: On paper the ground is the horizontal, so height must be stacked upward along the other axis.
senses.whyCN: 在纸面上地面是水平线，高度就只能沿着另一条轴向上堆叠。

senses.title: Of a structure's shape
senses.titleCN: 竖立的：形容建筑或结构的形态
senses.definition: standing upright rather than lying flat, as of a wall, cliff or column
senses.definitionCN: 指墙、崖壁、柱子等立起而非平躺的形态
senses.example: The climbers faced a vertical wall of wet rock.
senses.exampleCN: 攀登者面对的是湿滑岩壁的垂直面。
senses.why: The abstract direction becomes a physical surface; to climb it is to go up the same line.
senses.whyCN: 抽象方向变成了实体的面；攀爬它就是沿着同一条线往上走。

senses.title: Of organisation or movement
senses.titleCN: 纵向的：组织层级或垂直起降
senses.definition: describing organisation or motion that works up and down a hierarchy, or straight up into the air
senses.definitionCN: 形容沿层级上下运作的组织方式，或笔直向上的运动
senses.example: The plane can make a vertical take-off from the narrow deck.
senses.exampleCN: 这种飞机能从狭窄的甲板上垂直起飞。
senses.why: The same geometric line now describes power and motion: straight up, with no sideways step.
senses.whyCN: 同一条几何线此时描述权力与运动：笔直向上，不向旁侧迈步。

senses.title: The noun: the upright direction
senses.titleCN: 名词：垂直方向或垂直线
senses.definition: used as a noun for a vertical line, surface or position
senses.definitionCN: 作名词使用，指垂直线、垂直面或竖直位置
senses.example: The shelf rests exactly on the vertical.
senses.exampleCN: 架子正好贴着垂直线安放。
senses.why: The adjective steps into noun use, as English often lets it: the upright itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词用法，英语常常如此：指竖直本身。

intro.en: Vertical comes from Latin vertex, the crown of the head or the top point, which itself grew from the verb 'to turn'.
intro.cn: vertical 源自拉丁语 vertex，指头顶的旋或顶点，而后者又出自表示「转」的动词。

items.en: The verb vertere meant 'to turn'; a vertex is the point where something turns or peaks.
items.cn: 动词 vertere 意为「转」；vertex 就是事物转向或达到顶点的那一点。

items.en: Vertex meant 'whirlpool, crown of the head, summit, highest point'.
items.cn: vertex 意为「漩涡、头顶的旋、顶点、最高处」。

items.en: Late Latin verticalis meant 'of the highest point', and by extension 'overhead'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 verticalis 意为「顶点的」，引申为「正上方的」。

items.en: Astronomers used the vertical for the line straight overhead; the exact first use in this sense is uncertain.
items.cn: 天文学家借用 vertical 表示正上方的直线；这一义项的确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Geometry fixed the modern sense: perpendicular to the horizon, the opposite of horizontal.
items.cn: 几何学确立了现代义：与地平线成直角，与 horizontal 相对。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same vert- turning root; the near-meaning group gathers upright and perpendicular words.
note.cn: 形近组收同带 vert- 转根的词；近义组收表示竖直与垂直的词。

entries.definition: The top point or the corner where two lines meet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顶点」，指最高点或两条线相交的角点。

entries.definition: Lying flat, parallel to the horizon; the partner word that frames vertical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「水平的」，与 vertical 相对而彼此定义。

entries.definition: Moral goodness; a different Latin word, easily confused in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美德」，来自另一个拉丁词，拼写相近容易混。

entries.definition: Standing straight up; plainer and more physical than vertical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「竖直的、站直的」，比 vertical 更朴素、更具体。

entries.definition: Meeting a line or surface at a right angle; geometric and precise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「垂直的、成直角的」，更具几何精确性。

entries.definition: Exactly vertical, as checked with a weighted line.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「垂直的」，特指用铅垂线测得笔直。

entries.definition: Rising sharply, but not necessarily straight up.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「陡的」，形容坡面很斜，但未必竖直。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin vertex and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 vertex，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: vertical pairs with horizontal: one stands, the other lies flat.
normal.cn: vertical 与 horizontal 相对：一个立着，一个平躺。

normal.en: vertex is the top of the head; vertical is the line that points there.
normal.cn: vertex 是头顶的旋；vertical 就是指向那里的那条线。

normal.en: On a chart, the vertical axis shows height and the horizontal shows time.
normal.cn: 在图表上，纵轴表示高度，横轴表示时间。

normal.en: Vertical take-off means up, straight up, without a runway.
normal.cn: vertical take-off 意为不靠跑道、笔直向上起飞。

normal.en: A plumb line hangs to tell you whether a wall is truly vertical.
normal.cn: 铅垂线垂下来，用来判断墙是否真正垂直。

abstract.en: Picture a weighted string hanging beside a new brick wall; the wall is right only when it hugs the string.
abstract.cn: 想象一条挂着重物的线在新砌的砖墙旁垂下；墙只有贴着这条线才是正的。

abstract.en: The word is defined by contrast: nothing is vertical alone, only against something level.
abstract.cn: 这个词靠对比来定义：没有东西能独自垂直，只能相对于某个水平面。

abstract.en: The same line runs through geometry, buildings and graphs: up is one direction only.
abstract.cn: 同一条线贯穿几何、建筑和图表：向上的方向只有一个。

examples.en: Draw a vertical line down the middle of the page.
examples.cn: 在页面中央画一条垂直线。

examples.en: The cliff is almost vertical for the last hundred metres.
examples.cn: 最后一百米，那面崖壁几乎完全垂直。

examples.en: The vertical axis shows the number of visitors each month.
examples.cn: 纵轴表示每个月的游客人数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我（ver）提（ti）抠（cal）」——我提着一根线往下抠，看墙正不正：垂直的

root: 源自拉丁语 vertex「头顶的旋、顶点」，出自动词 vertere「转」，晚期拉丁语 verticalis「顶点的」；经科学拉丁语进入英语；同族词有 vertex、convert、version。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of vertical hold one line upright: a geometric direction, a graph axis, a standing surface, an upward movement, and finally the upright itself as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: vertical 的五个义项守着同一条竖直的线：几何方向、图表轴、立起的表面、向上的运动，最后是作为名词的「竖直」本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plumb line hangs beside a fresh wall, and the wall is right only if it hugs the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：铅垂线在新墙旁垂下，墙贴着这条线才算正。

branches.en: GEOMETRY LINE: straight up and down, at a right angle to the ground.
branches.cn: 几何线：笔直上下，与地面成直角。

branches.en: GRAPH LINE: the height axis of a chart.
branches.cn: 图表线：图表中的高度轴。

branches.en: SURFACE LINE: walls and cliffs that stand up to be climbed.
branches.cn: 表面线：立起来可以攀爬的墙与崖壁。

branches.en: MOTION LINE: lifting straight up, or power moving up and down a hierarchy.
branches.cn: 运动线：笔直向上升起，或权力沿层级上下运行。

branches.en: NOUN LINE: the upright itself, used as a thing.
branches.cn: 名词线：竖直本身被当作一个事物来用。

intro.en: Vertical is a Latin adjective stem with an English -al ending, built on the turning root vert-.
intro.cn: vertical 是拉丁语形容词词干接英语 -al 词尾，建立在「转」这个词根 vert- 上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vertex and verticalis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：vertex 与 verticalis。

items.example: It forms the paired word horizontal.
It forms verticals in technical use.
items.exampleCN: 它在技术语境中构成 verticals。

definition_zh: 船、舰；容器、器皿；（体内的）血管、导管
definition_en: a ship or large boat, a hollow container for liquid, or a tube that carries blood or other fluid in the body
core_image: 一个中空的器皿，能装水，也能载人渡海
scene: 港湾里停着一艘旧货船，甲板上的木桶正被吊下船。A small vessel carried the crew back to the shore at dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 vessel 是「船、舰」（第 1 个义项：水上交通运输工具）；句意为黄昏时一艘小船把船员送回岸边。水上能载人的那个容器，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：船、舰；容器、器皿；血管、导管

derivatives.zh: 加 -ed 构成，义为「有容器的；装了器皿的」（罕见）
同一拉丁词源 vas 的后代，义为「花瓶」
拉丁语原词，义为「容器」，是解剖学 vas deferens 的第一部分

senses.title: A ship or large boat
senses.titleCN: 船、舰：水上往来的大型运载工具
senses.definition: a ship or large boat, especially one used for trade or war
senses.definitionCN: 船或大型艇，尤指用于贸易或军事的
senses.example: A cargo vessel left the port before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天还没亮，一艘货船就离港了。
senses.why: Latin vas means a container; a ship is the container people live in while crossing water.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vas 意为「容器」；船就是人们渡水时居住其中的那个容器。

senses.title: A container for liquid
senses.titleCN: 容器：盛放液体的器皿
senses.definition: a hollow container, especially one used for holding liquids
senses.definitionCN: 中空的容器，尤指盛放液体的器皿
senses.example: The priest poured oil from a clay vessel.
senses.exampleCN: 祭司从一个陶器里倒出油。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word: something hollow that holds what is put inside.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层：中空之物，把放进去的东西盛住。

senses.title: A tube in the body
senses.titleCN: 血管、导管：体内的输送管道
senses.definition: a tube or duct in the body that carries blood or another fluid
senses.definitionCN: 体内输送血液或其他液体的管道
senses.example: Cold makes the blood vessels in the fingers narrow.
senses.exampleCN: 寒冷会让手指的血管收缩。
senses.why: The body borrows the container image: the tube holds and moves fluid the way a jug does.
senses.whyCN: 身体借用了容器意象：管道盛住并输送液体，正像一只水罐。

senses.title: A person as a bearer
senses.titleCN: （引申）承载者：作为载体的那个人
senses.definition: a person regarded as a bearer of a quality, a message or a role
senses.definitionCN: 被看作承载某种品质、信息或角色的人
senses.example: In the old story the youngest son is the vessel of the family's hope.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个老故事里，最小的儿子承载着全家的希望。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from thing to person: whoever holds and carries something onward is a vessel for it.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从物移到人：任何盛住并把某物传递下去的人，都是它的容器。

senses.title: A boat in a fixed sense
senses.titleCN: 固定说法中的「艇」
senses.definition: used in fixed names for types of boat, such as a patrol vessel or a research vessel
senses.definitionCN: 用于巡逻艇、科考船等固定船名说法中
senses.example: A research vessel spent three months mapping the sea floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一艘科考船花了三个月测绘海底。
senses.why: Here the container idea is frozen into a name for a job at sea.
senses.whyCN: 此时容器观念已经固化成一个命名海上职务的说法。

intro.en: Vessel came from Latin through Old French, and every sense still carries the idea of something hollow that holds.
intro.cn: vessel 经古法语来自拉丁语，每个义项都还带着「中空能盛」的观念。

items.en: Vas meant 'vessel, container, dish'; the plural vasa is still used in anatomy.
items.cn: vas 意为「容器、器皿、盘碟」，其复数 vasa 至今仍在解剖学中使用。

items.en: The diminutive vascellum meant 'a small vessel', and it is the form that reached French.
items.cn: 指小形式 vascellum 意为「小容器」，正是传到法语的那一形式。

items.en: Old French vaisseau meant both a container and a ship, keeping the two ideas together.
items.cn: 古法语 vaisseau 同时指容器与船，把两个观念放在一处。

items.en: English borrowed vessel in the thirteenth century, with ship, container and body-tube senses all present.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 vessel，船、容器与体内管道三个义项当时都已具备。

items.en: Nautical and medical usage split the word: a fishing vessel and a blood vessel barely meet.
items.cn: 航海与医学用法把这个词分开：渔船与血管几乎互不相干。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same container family; the near-meaning group gathers ships and containers with different shades.
note.cn: 形近组收同一容器词族的词；近义组收船只与容器类词，彼此侧重不同。

entries.definition: A decorative container for flowers; the Latin vas survives here too.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「花瓶」，同样来自拉丁语 vas。

entries.definition: The Latin word for vessel, used in anatomical terms such as vas deferens.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语原词，意为容器，用于 vas deferens 等解剖学术语。

entries.definition: A person who owes loyalty to a lord; an unrelated medieval word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「封臣」，来自中古拉丁语，与本词只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A large seagoing vessel; the general word beside the more formal vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「船」，是最通用的说法，vessel 更正式。

entries.definition: A smaller craft; vessel usually implies something larger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小船」，vessel 通常指更大的船。

entries.definition: Anything that holds something; broader and plainer than vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「容器」，比 vessel 更宽泛、更朴素。

entries.definition: A tube in the body or a building; the clinical partner of vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「导管」，是 vessel 在医学语境中的伙伴词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin vas and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 vas，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: One word, three holders: a vessel carries people, water or blood.
normal.cn: 一个词，三种盛器：vessel 载人、盛水、运血。

normal.en: Latin vas is a container; a ship is a container you sail in.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vas 是容器；船就是你在里面航行的容器。

normal.en: Blood vessel and fishing vessel share the same shape of idea.
normal.cn: 血管与渔船共用同一个形状的观念。

normal.en: Vessel is more formal than ship; officials say vessel.
normal.cn: vessel 比 ship 更正式，官方文件多用 vessel。

normal.en: A vessel must be hollow: the inside matters more than the outside.
normal.cn: 器皿必须是中空的：里面比外面更重要。

abstract.en: Picture a clay jug on a table: the empty space is the useful part, and the clay only holds it.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上的一只陶罐：真正有用的是中间的空处，陶土只是把它围住。

abstract.en: The word then fills that emptiness with different contents: grain, oil, people, blood.
abstract.cn: 这个词随后用不同的内容填满那片空：谷物、油、人、血。

abstract.en: Anything that carries something safely across a distance can be called a vessel.
abstract.cn: 任何能把某物安全运送过一段距离的东西，都可以称为 vessel。

examples.en: A rescue vessel reached the sinking boat within twenty minutes.
examples.cn: 一艘救援船在二十分钟内赶到了那艘下沉的船旁。

examples.en: Store the oil in a sealed vessel away from heat.
examples.cn: 把油存放在远离热源的密封容器里。

examples.en: The doctor said the vessels around his heart were narrow.
examples.cn: 医生说他心脏周围的血管变窄了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维（ve）塞尔（ssel）」——维塞尔港口的船，一只会装货的大器皿：船；容器

root: 源自拉丁语 vas「容器」的指小形式 vascellum，经古法语 vaisseau「容器、船」进入英语；同源词有 vase、vas。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of vessel all share one hollow shape: a ship carrying people, a jug carrying liquid, a tube carrying blood, and by metaphor a person who carries a hope.
sensesIntro.cn: vessel 的五个义项共用同一个中空形状：船载人、罐盛液、管道运送血液，再经比喻指承载希望的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clay jug on a table, its hollow centre holding what is poured in.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的一只陶罐，中空处盛住倒进去的东西。

branches.en: CONTAINER LINE: the oldest layer, the jug on the table.
branches.cn: 容器线：最古老的一层，桌上的罐子。

branches.en: WATER LINE: the container grows large enough to sail in.
branches.cn: 水面线：容器大到可以航行其中，就成了船。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the same tube shape inside the body.
branches.cn: 体内线：身体内部同样的管状形态。

branches.en: METAPHOR LINE: a person becomes the vessel of a quality.
branches.cn: 比喻线：人成了某种品质的载体。

branches.en: CONTRAST: ship is plainer, vessel more formal and broader.
branches.cn: 对照线：ship 更朴素，vessel 更正式且范围更广。

intro.en: Vessel is a Latin diminutive that passed through French; the -el ending is a small reminder of its 'little container' origin.
intro.cn: vessel 是经法语而来的拉丁语指小形式；结尾 -el 隐约提示它「小容器」的出身。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vas, with the diminutive vascellum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：vas 及其指小形式 vascellum。

definition_zh: 病房；（城市的）区；受监护人；动词：挡开、避开
definition_en: a room or section of a hospital for patients, a district of a city, or to keep something away
core_image: 护士守在一间病人集中的房间里，门帘拉上，把外面的喧闹挡在门外
scene: 夜班的走廊很静，只有三号病房的灯还亮着。The children's ward was quiet, except for one child who could not sleep.
sceneCN: 这里 ward 是「病房」（第 1 个义项：医院里供病人集中的房间）；句意为儿童病房很安静，只有一个孩子睡不着。一间被帘子隔开、把喧闹挡在门外的房间，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：病房；城区；受监护的人（ward of court）
动词：挡开、避开（ward off）

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「看守；狱警」
同一词根加 -en 构成，义为「管理员；看守人」
由 ward 与 robe 复合而成，义为「衣柜；全部衣物」
与 ward 同源，义为「守卫；卫兵」

senses.title: A hospital room for patients
senses.titleCN: 病房：医院里病人集中的房间
senses.definition: a large room in a hospital where several patients are cared for
senses.definitionCN: 医院中同时照料多位病人的大房间
senses.example: She was moved to a ward on the second floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她被转到了二楼的病房。
senses.why: The old verb meant to guard; a ward is the space kept and watched over by nurses.
senses.whyCN: 古义「看守」是这个字根；ward 就是护士守着、看着的那片空间。

senses.title: A district of a city
senses.titleCN: 城区：城市划分出的一个区域
senses.definition: an area of a city or town used as a unit for elections or local government
senses.definitionCN: 城市或城镇的一个区域，用作选举或地方行政单位
senses.example: Each ward elects one member of the council.
senses.exampleCN: 每个选区选出一名议会议员。
senses.why: A district is also a space kept and watched, this time by a local official.
senses.whyCN: 城区同样是被人看守、照管的一片空间，只不过看守者换成了地方官员。

senses.title: A person under protection
senses.titleCN: 受监护人：由他人或法庭监护的人
senses.definition: a person, especially a child, placed under the legal care of a guardian or a court
senses.definitionCN: 被置于监护人或法庭法律照管之下的人，尤指儿童
senses.example: As a ward of court, the boy needed a judge's permission to travel.
senses.exampleCN: 作为由法庭监护的孩子，他出国需要法官批准。
senses.why: Guardianship comes full circle here: the guarded space becomes the guarded person.
senses.whyCN: 监护义在这里走了一个圆：被看守的空间变成了被看守的人。

senses.title: To keep something away
senses.titleCN: 挡开：把某物阻挡在外
senses.definition: in the phrase ward off, to prevent something harmful from reaching you
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 ward off，指阻止有害之物接近自己
senses.example: She waved her hand to ward off the flies.
senses.exampleCN: 她挥手把苍蝇挡开。
senses.why: The verb restores the original guarding action: the arm and the charm stand between you and harm.
senses.whyCN: 动词恢复了最初的看守动作：手臂与护符拦在你和伤害之间。

senses.title: As a suffix in compound words
senses.titleCN: 作后缀：构成方向或对象的复合词
senses.definition: used as a suffix in words such as homeward and backward, marking direction
senses.definitionCN: 用作 homeward、backward 等词的后缀，表示方向
senses.example: The road homeward was longer than he remembered.
senses.exampleCN: 回家的路比他记忆中的更长。
senses.why: The same Old English element shifted from 'keeping watch' to 'turning toward', a change the etymologists still discuss.
senses.whyCN: 同一古英语成分从「守望」转向「朝向」，这一变化至今仍为词源学者讨论。

intro.en: Ward is an Old English word for keeping watch, and the modern senses all grow out of guarded space and guarded people.
intro.cn: ward 是古英语中表示「守望」的词，现代各义项都由「被看守的空间」与「被看守的人」生长出来。

items.en: Weard meant 'a watch, a guarding'; the verb weardian meant to guard or occupy.
items.cn: weard 意为「守望、守卫」，动词 weardian 意为看守或占据。

items.en: Related forms in Old Saxon and Old High German share the guarding sense, so the root is very old.
items.cn: 古撒克逊语与古高地德语中的相关形式同样表示看守，可见这一词根极为古老。

items.en: The word came to name a guarded place: a district watched by an officer, and later a room watched by nurses.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐指被看守的地方：先是由官员管辖的城区，后是由护士照看的房间。

items.en: By c. 1300 a ward of court was a minor under the court's protection, the guarded person.
items.cn: 约在 1300 年，ward of court 指受法庭保护、被照管的未成年人。

items.en: The phrase ward off kept the original action alive, while the -ward suffix developed its direction sense.
items.cn: 短语 ward off 保住了最初的动作义，而 -ward 后缀则发展出方向义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers guarding words of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers hospital rooms and city districts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的看守类词；近义组收病房与城区的相关说法。

entries.definition: To protect or watch over; the French-shaped twin of ward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「守卫、卫兵」，是 ward 的法语形孪生词。

entries.definition: An official who watches over a building, a park or prisoners.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理员、看守长」，指看守建筑、园区或囚犯的人。

entries.definition: A prison officer; the person who does the guarding.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「狱警、看守」。

entries.definition: In the direction of; -ward here marks direction, not guarding.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「朝向」，此处的 -ward 表方向而非看守。

entries.definition: A place for medical advice or treatment, often smaller than a hospital ward.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「诊所」，通常比病房所在科室小。

entries.definition: An area of a town or country, the everyday word beside ward.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「地区、区域」，是 ward 在城区义上的日常说法。

entries.definition: To push away or look after oneself; often in fend off.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挡开、照料自己」，多用于 fend off。

entries.definition: To drive something back by force; stronger than ward off.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「击退」，比 ward off 语气更强。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English weard and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 weard，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: ward and guard are one word in two shapes: one English, one French.
normal.cn: ward 与 guard 是同一个词的两副面孔：一个英语形，一个法语形。

normal.en: A ward is a space watched over; a warden is the person who watches.
normal.cn: ward 是被看守的空间；warden 是看守的人。

normal.en: Ward off keeps the original meaning: hold the harm outside.
normal.cn: ward off 保留了本义：把伤害挡在外面。

normal.en: The children's ward, the maternity ward: names for groups of patients in one room.
normal.cn: 儿童病房、产科病房：都是同一间房里一群病人的名字。

normal.en: Each city ward elects its own councillor.
normal.cn: 城市的每个选区各自选出议员。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain drawn across a hospital bay: inside is watched, outside is shut out, and both are ward.
abstract.cn: 想象病房里拉上一道帘子：里面被照看，外面被隔开，两者都是 ward。

abstract.en: The word moves from the watchman to the place watched, and then to the person watched over.
abstract.cn: 这个词从守望者移到被守望的地方，再移到被照看的人。

abstract.en: Warding off is the smallest form of guarding: one raised arm against a fly.
abstract.cn: 挡开是最小形式的看守：一条抬起的手臂挡住一只苍蝇。

examples.en: The nurse checked every bed in the ward before midnight.
examples.cn: 护士在午夜前查看了病房里的每一张床。

examples.en: He lit a fire to ward off the cold.
examples.cn: 他生起火来御寒。

examples.en: The city is divided into twelve wards for local elections.
examples.cn: 这座城市为地方选举划分为十二个选区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我（war）的（d）」——我的地盘我守着，一间病人住着的房间：病房；守望

root: 古英语 weard「守望、守卫」，动词 weardian「看守」；与 guard 同源，-ward 后缀亦出自同一成分；派生词有 warden、warder、wardrobe。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of ward travel from the guarding act to the place guarded, the district, the person guarded, the act of keeping harm away, and finally the direction suffix.
sensesIntro.cn: ward 的五个义项从看守动作出发，依次走到被看守的空间、城区、被看守的人、把伤害挡开的动作，最后是表方向的后缀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curtain drawn across a hospital bay, the inside watched, the outside shut away.
core.cn: 核心意象：病房里拉上的帘子，里面被照看，外面被隔开。

branches.en: ROOM LINE: the space nurses keep watch over.
branches.cn: 房间线：护士守望的那片空间。

branches.en: MAP LINE: the city is cut into wards, each watched by an officer.
branches.cn: 地图线：城市被切成若干区，每区由官员管辖。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: the guarded space becomes a guarded child.
branches.cn: 人物线：被看守的空间变成了被照看的孩子。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: ward off brings back the original raised arm.
branches.cn: 动作线：ward off 带回最初抬起的手臂。

branches.en: SUFFIX LINE: the same element turns into a direction marker.
branches.cn: 后缀线：同一成分转为方向标记。

intro.en: Ward is a native Old English word; its 'affixes' are really its own suffixes, which also appear across the language.
intro.cn: ward 是本族古英语词；这里所谓的词缀其实是它自身的后缀成分，同样通行于其他词中。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 warden 与 warder。

definition_zh: 温暖的；暖和的；热情的；动词：使暖和、加热
definition_en: fairly hot in a pleasant way, friendly and enthusiastic, or to make something slightly hotter
core_image: 双手捧住一杯刚倒的热茶，指尖一点点回暖
scene: 冬天的厨房窗户起了雾，灶上的水正冒着热气。She wrapped both hands around the warm cup and stopped shivering.
sceneCN: 这里 warm 是「温暖的、暖和的」（第 1 个义项：温度适中而令人舒适）；句意为她双手捧住暖和的杯子，不再发抖。捧着热杯回温的感觉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：温暖的；暖和的；热情的、亲切的
动词：使暖和；加热；变得热情

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -th 构成，义为「温暖；热情」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「温暖地；热情地」
由比较级转为名词，义为「加热器；暖手器」
加 -ing 构成，义为「变暖；加温」

senses.title: Pleasantly hot
senses.titleCN: 温暖的：温度舒服地偏高
senses.definition: fairly hot, especially in a way that feels pleasant rather than uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 温度较高，尤其令人舒适而不难受
senses.example: The bread was still warm from the oven.
senses.exampleCN: 面包刚从炉子里出来，还热着。
senses.why: Old English wearm described a moderate heat, and the word has always kept that comfort, not the extreme.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wearm 指适中的热度，这个词一直保留着舒适感，而不指极端。

senses.title: Of clothing or shelter
senses.titleCN: 保暖的：衣物或住处不易散失热量
senses.definition: keeping the body heat in, as of clothes, rooms or bedding
senses.definitionCN: 能留住体温的，如衣服、房间或被褥
senses.example: Take a warm coat; the wind is sharp tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 带上件厚外套，今晚风很刺骨。
senses.why: The same moderate heat is held close to the body, so the adjective moves from air to clothing.
senses.whyCN: 同一种适中的热度被留在身体旁边，于是形容词从空气转移到衣物上。

senses.title: Friendly and enthusiastic
senses.titleCN: 热情的：态度亲切而热烈
senses.definition: showing friendliness, affection or enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 表现出友善、亲近或热忱
senses.example: They gave the visitors a warm welcome at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门口热情地欢迎来访者。
senses.why: Warmth in the body became warmth in manner: a person who makes you comfortable is metaphorically warm.
senses.whyCN: 身上的温暖变成了态度上的温暖：让人感到舒适的人，在比喻意义上就是 warm。

senses.title: To make slightly hotter
senses.titleCN: 加热：使某物稍热一些
senses.definition: to make something warmer, or to become warmer
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变暖，或自身变暖
senses.example: Warm the milk gently before adding the honey.
senses.exampleCN: 加蜂蜜之前先把牛奶稍稍加热。
senses.why: The adjective turns into the action that produces it: heat is applied a little at a time.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成产生它的动作：热被一点一点地加上去。

senses.title: To become friendly toward
senses.titleCN: 变得喜欢：对某人某事生出好感
senses.definition: in phrases like warm to, to begin to like or feel friendly toward something
senses.definitionCN: 用于 warm to 等短语，指开始喜欢或对某事产生好感
senses.example: The audience warmed to her after the second song.
senses.exampleCN: 第二首歌之后，观众开始喜欢上她。
senses.why: Friendliness is again heat, but now rising slowly, as a cold room warms up.
senses.whyCN: 友善再度成了热，只不过这次是慢慢升起的，像一间冷屋子渐渐暖起来。

intro.en: Warm is an old Germanic word, and its relatives run all through northern Europe.
intro.cn: warm 是古老的日耳曼语词，它的同源词遍布北欧各语言。

items.en: Wearm meant 'warm, not cold', and also appeared in compounds for warm-hearted feeling.
items.cn: wearm 意为「暖的、不冷的」，也出现在表示热心的复合词中。

items.en: The root is reconstructed as a word for being warm; German warm and Dutch warm are exact cognates.
items.cn: 这个词根被重构为「温暖」之义；德语 warm 与荷兰语 warm 是精确同源词。

items.en: Deeper connections to Latin formus 'warm' are debated, and the further origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 它与拉丁语 formus「暖的」之间更深的关系仍有争议，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The spelling settled as warm, and the verb use, to warm something, was already common.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 warm，动词用法「使暖和」当时已很常见。

items.en: Idioms extended the word: warm up for exercise, warm to an idea, a warm welcome.
items.cn: 习语进一步扩展了它：warm up 热身、warm to 产生好感、warm welcome 热情欢迎。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers temperature words close in shape; the near-meaning group gathers degrees and kinds of heat.
note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的温度词；近义组收不同程度与不同性质的热。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being warm, and for friendly feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「温暖；热情」，指暖的性质与友善情感。

entries.definition: A device or garment that keeps something warm; also the comparative.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指保暖的器具或衣物；也是比较级形式。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something in a warm or friendly way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「温暖地；热情地」。

entries.definition: Gentle exercise before a sport or performance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「热身运动」。

entries.definition: At a high temperature, often uncomfortable; far stronger than warm.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「热的」，温度高且常令人不适，比 warm 强得多。

entries.definition: Only slightly warm, and by extension unenthusiastic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「微温的」，引申为「不热心的」。

entries.definition: Snug and comfortable; the feeling of warmth rather than its degree.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「舒适暖和的」，侧重感受而非温度。

entries.definition: Made hot deliberately; also describes an angry argument.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「加热的」，也形容激烈的争论。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wearm and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wearm，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: warm sits between cool and hot: pleasant heat, not a burn.
normal.cn: warm 位于 cool 与 hot 之间：是舒服的热，不会烫。

normal.en: A warm welcome borrows the body's comfort for the manners.
normal.cn: a warm welcome 借身体的舒适来形容待客之道。

normal.en: Warm up first, or the muscles will complain.
normal.cn: 先 warm up 热身，否则肌肉会抱怨。

normal.en: Lukewarm adds a lukewarm middle: only slightly warm, and not keen.
normal.cn: lukewarm 在中间加了一层：只是微温，也不太热心。

normal.en: Warmth is the noun; warmly is how a warm person acts.
normal.cn: warmth 是名词；warmly 是热情的人做事的方式。

abstract.en: Picture two cupped hands around a mug: the word is a small, safe heat you can hold.
abstract.cn: 想象双手捧住一只杯子：这个词是可以握住的、安全的小小热度。

abstract.en: The same rise in temperature serves both skin and feeling, so friendliness is spoken of as heat.
abstract.cn: 同一种温度上升同时服务于皮肤与情感，于是友善被说成热度。

abstract.en: Warmth is always comparative in practice: warm relative to the air, the room, or the person.
abstract.cn: 温暖在实践中总是相对的：相对于空气、房间或那个人。

examples.en: The stone wall stayed warm long after sunset.
examples.cn: 日落很久之后，那面石墙还是暖的。

examples.en: She warmed her hands over the small stove.
examples.cn: 她把手放在小炉子上取暖。

examples.en: The villagers gave the teachers a warm welcome.
examples.cn: 村民们热情地欢迎这些老师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我母」——我母亲的手总是暖的：温暖的

root: 古英语 wearm「暖的」，源自日耳曼语同一词根，与德语 warm、荷兰语 warm 同源；派生词有 warmth、warmly、warmer。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of warm share one moderate heat: pleasant air, clothing that keeps it, a friendly manner, the act of adding heat, and finally the slow warming of affection.
sensesIntro.cn: warm 的五个义项共用同一种适中的热：宜人的空气、留热的衣物、亲切的态度、加热的动作，最后是感情慢慢变暖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands cupped around a mug of hot tea, fingers slowly coming back to life.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手捧住一杯热茶，指尖慢慢回温。

branches.en: AIR LINE: heat that feels good on the skin.
branches.cn: 空气线：皮肤上觉得舒服的热。

branches.en: CLOTHING LINE: heat held close to the body.
branches.cn: 衣物线：紧贴身体留住的热。

branches.en: FEELING LINE: friendliness, and its slow rising.
branches.cn: 情感线：亲切，以及它缓慢的升温。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: heat applied a little at a time.
branches.cn: 动作线：一点一点加上的热。

branches.en: CONTRAST: hot burns, warm comforts, lukewarm disappoints.
branches.cn: 对照线：hot 烫，warm 舒服，lukewarm 让人失望。

intro.en: Warm is a native Germanic word; the endings it takes are ordinary English suffixes.
intro.cn: warm 是本族日耳曼语词；它接的都是普通英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 警告；提醒；告诫；预先通知
definition_en: to tell someone about a possible danger or problem so that they can avoid it
core_image: 一个人伸手拦住同伴，指着前方，要他在踏出下一步之前先停下
scene: 山路边的牌子被风吹得咣咣响，护林员在岔口拦住游客。He warned us that the path would be icy after dark.
sceneCN: 这里 warn 是「警告、提醒」（第 1 个义项：告知可能发生的危险，以便对方避开）；句意为他提醒我们天黑后小路会结冰。伸手拦住同伴的动作，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：警告、告诫；提醒；预先通知

collocations.zh: 受到警告；要有心理准备

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「警告；警告信号」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「已受警告的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「警告者；报警装置」
加前缀 fore- 构成，义为「预先警告」

senses.title: To tell of danger
senses.titleCN: 警告：告知有危险
senses.definition: to tell someone about a danger or problem before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在危险或问题发生之前告诉某人
senses.example: The coastguard warned the boats about the coming storm.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸警卫队警告船只将有暴风雨来袭。
senses.why: Old English warnian meant to take heed and to admonish; the word names the act of making someone careful before harm arrives.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 warnian 意为留心与告诫；这个词指在伤害到来之前使人警醒的动作。

senses.title: To advise against
senses.titleCN: 告诫：劝人不要做某事
senses.definition: to advise someone strongly not to do something
senses.definitionCN: 强烈劝告某人不要做某事
senses.example: Doctors warn against taking the pills on an empty stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 医生告诫不要空腹服用这些药片。
senses.why: The same forward look is aimed at an action: the danger is what the doing would bring, so the advice is a prohibition.
senses.whyCN: 同样是对未来的注视，只是这次落在某个动作上：危险正是这个动作会带来的，所以劝告成了禁令。

senses.title: To give notice in advance
senses.titleCN: 预先通知：提前告知某事会来
senses.definition: to inform someone in advance that something is going to happen
senses.definitionCN: 提前告知某人某事即将发生
senses.example: Nobody warned me that the office would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人提前告诉我办公室会提前关门。
senses.why: With danger taken out, only the timing remains: the word still speaks of a thing before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 把危险抽掉之后，只剩下时间关系：这个词说的仍是事情发生之前的那一句话。

senses.title: To caution officially
senses.titleCN: 正式警告：由权威出面告诫
senses.definition: to caution a person officially, especially about behaviour or breaking a rule
senses.definitionCN: 由官方或权威出面告诫某人，尤指其行为或违规
senses.example: The referee warned the player before showing the card.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判在出示牌之前先警告了这名球员。
senses.why: An authority repeats the hedge at the cliff edge in a formal voice, and the next step is a penalty.
senses.whyCN: 权威以正式的口吻重演崖边那道拦阻，而下一步就是处罚。

senses.title: To keep someone off
senses.titleCN: 警告离开：阻止某人靠近
senses.definition: in the phrase warn off, to tell someone to stay away from a place or a person
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 warn off，令某人远离某地或某人
senses.example: The farmer warned the walkers off the closed field.
senses.exampleCN: 农场主警告散步的人离开那片封闭的田地。
senses.why: Here the warning becomes a wall of words: the message is not what to watch but where not to stand.
senses.whyCN: 此时警告变成了一道用话砌成的墙：信息不是该注意什么，而是不该站在哪里。

intro.en: Warn comes from an Old English word for refusing or forbidding, and it is close kin to 'beware'.
intro.cn: warn 来自古英语中表示「拒绝、禁止」的词，与 beware 关系很近。

items.en: Warnian meant 'to take heed, be careful', and also 'to admonish or forbid'.
items.cn: warnian 意为「留心、当心」，也表示「告诫、禁止」。

items.en: The noun waru meant 'care, protection, guard', part of the same Germanic cluster.
items.cn: 名词 waru 意为「注意、保护、看守」，属于同一日耳曼词群。

items.en: German warnen 'to warn' and Dutch waarschuwen in part share this history.
items.cn: 德语 warnen 与荷兰语的部分说法共享这段历史。

items.en: The shorter form warn came from the infinitive warnian, and the beware sense drifted to the separate word beware.
items.cn: 较短形式 warn 出自不定式 warnian，而「当心」这一义则漂移到独立词 beware 上。

items.en: The present range runs from a shout at a cliff edge to a formal letter from a court.
items.cn: 现代用法从崖边的呼喊一直到法庭的正式函件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the warn / war shape; the near-meaning group gathers ways of telling people about risk.
note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的 warn、war 类词；近义组收告知风险的多种说法。

entries.definition: A statement or sign that tells of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警告；警示」，指告知危险的话语或标志。

entries.definition: To be careful of something; the old be-wary sense kept as its own word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「当心」，把古老的「警觉」义保存为独立词。

entries.definition: The past participle of wear, meaning used or damaged; a homophone trap.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，是 wear 的过去分词，意为磨损的；与本词同音，是易混点。

entries.definition: To twist out of shape; an unrelated word of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「翘曲、扭曲」，与本词只是形近，来源无关。

entries.definition: To tell someone to be ready for danger; often brief and urgent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使警觉」，多用于简短紧急的提醒。

entries.definition: To tell someone to be careful, often in a gentler or official tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「告诫」，语气较轻或偏正式。

entries.definition: To state an intention to harm; the warning becomes hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「威胁」，警告在此变成了敌意。

entries.definition: To give someone advice about what to do; warmer and less about danger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建议」，语气更和气，重点不在危险。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English warnian and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 warnian，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Warn, not scold: the point is to stop something before it hurts.
normal.cn: warn 不是责骂：要点是在造成伤害之前拦住它。

normal.en: Warn of a thing, warn against an action: the preposition shows the target.
normal.cn: warn of 后接事物，warn against 后接动作：介词显示对象。

normal.en: Beware carries the old careful sense of warn away as its own word.
normal.cn: beware 把 warn 古老的「当心」义带走，成了独立词。

normal.en: A warning can be a word, a sign or a red light.
normal.cn: warning 可以是一句话、一块标志牌或一盏红灯。

normal.en: Worn is a homophone and means used up: do not mix the two.
normal.cn: worn 是同音词，意为磨旧的：不要混用。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a companion's chest at the edge of a cliff: the body stops first, the explanation comes after.
abstract.cn: 想象在崖边一只手按住同伴的胸口：身体先停下，解释随后才来。

abstract.en: The word faces forward in time: it only works if heard before the harm.
abstract.cn: 这个词朝向未来：只有在伤害之前被听见，它才起作用。

abstract.en: From a shout to a printed notice to a court letter, the same forward-looking alarm.
abstract.cn: 从一声呼喊到一张通告，再到一封法庭来函，是同一种前瞻性的警报。

examples.en: The guide warned us that the bridge might be unsafe.
examples.cn: 导游提醒我们那座桥可能不安全。

examples.en: Doctors warn against skipping breakfast every day.
examples.cn: 医生告诫不要每天都不吃早饭。

examples.en: A red light warns drivers when the crossing is busy.
examples.cn: 人行横道忙碌时，红灯会提醒司机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「网」——路边拉了红色警示网，提醒你别再往前走：警告

root: 古英语 warnian「留心、告诫、禁止」，与 waru「注意、保护」同属一个日耳曼词群；beware 保存了其中「当心」的一支；派生词有 warning、forewarn。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of warn all face forward in time: danger ahead, an action to avoid, news in advance, official caution, and a call to keep away.
sensesIntro.cn: warn 的五个义项都朝向未来：前方的危险、要避开的动作、提前的通告、正式的告诫，以及令人远离的喝止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out against a companion's chest at the edge of a cliff.
core.cn: 核心意象：崖边一只横在同伴胸前的手。

branches.en: DANGER LINE: the word points at what is coming.
branches.cn: 危险线：这个词指着即将到来的东西。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: the advice is aimed at what not to do.
branches.cn: 动作线：劝告落在不该做的事上。

branches.en: NOTICE LINE: the warning may be plain information in advance.
branches.cn: 通知线：警告也可能只是提前告知信息。

branches.en: AUTHORITY LINE: an official voice repeats the same caution.
branches.cn: 权威线：官方声音重复同样的告诫。

branches.en: DISTANCE LINE: warn off pushes the person away.
branches.cn: 距离线：warn off 把人推得更远。

intro.en: Warn is a native verb; its relatives in English are the endings it takes and the beware branch.
intro.cn: warn 是本族动词；它在英语中的亲属是所接的词尾以及 beware 这一分支。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.

items.exampleCN: 它与本词同属一个词群。

definition_zh: 洗；洗涤；冲洗；（水）冲刷；名词：洗；待洗的衣物
definition_en: to clean something with water and usually soap, or the act of cleaning this way
core_image: 一盆水被搅动，脏东西被水带走，露出底下干净的一层
scene: 傍晚的院子里，母亲把沾满泥的孩子的手按进盆里来回搓。Wash your hands before you sit down at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 wash 是「洗、洗涤」（第 1 个义项：用水和肥皂把东西弄干净）；句意为坐到桌前先把手洗干净。把脏东西用水带走，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：洗、洗涤；冲洗；冲刷
名词：洗；洗过的衣物；（水的）冲刷

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「洗涤；待洗的衣物」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「洗衣机；垫圈」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可水洗的」
复合词，义为「洗手间」

senses.title: To clean with water
senses.titleCN: 洗：用水把东西弄干净
senses.definition: to clean something with water, usually with soap
senses.definitionCN: 用水清洗某物，通常加肥皂
senses.example: She washed the dusty cups under the tap.
senses.exampleCN: 她在水龙头下把积尘的杯子洗了。
senses.why: Old English wascan meant to wash, and the whole family in northern Europe carries the same simple action.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wascan 意为「洗」，北欧各语言的同源词都指向这一简单动作。

senses.title: To clean a body part
senses.titleCN: 洗（身体某部位）：把身上的脏东西去掉
senses.definition: to clean a part of the body, especially the hands or face
senses.definitionCN: 清洗身体的某一部分，尤指手和脸
senses.example: He washed his face in the cold stream.
senses.exampleCN: 他在冰冷的溪水里洗了脸。
senses.why: The object here is one's own body, so the verb often appears without a separate thing being washed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对象是自己的身子，所以动词常不另带被洗的东西。

senses.title: To carry away by water
senses.titleCN: 冲走：水流把东西带走
senses.definition: of water, to carry something away or to flow against a shore
senses.definitionCN: 指水流把东西带走，或拍打冲刷岸边
senses.example: The flood washed the bridge away in one night.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水一夜之间把桥冲走了。
senses.why: The same verb without soap: water still removes what it touches, only now nothing is cleaned.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词，不加肥皂：水依然带走它碰到的东西，只是这次什么都没被洗净。

senses.title: The act of washing
senses.titleCN: 洗：洗一次这件事
senses.definition: the act or occasion of cleaning with water
senses.definitionCN: 用水清洗的一次行为或场合
senses.example: The curtains could use a good wash.
senses.exampleCN: 这些窗帘该好好洗一次了。
senses.why: The verb turns into a countable noun, so the cleaning becomes something you can give a thing.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为名词，可以计数，于是清洗变成能给某物的一次处理。

senses.title: Clothes to be washed
senses.titleCN: 待洗的衣物：一堆要洗的东西
senses.definition: in the phrase the wash, the clothes and other items waiting to be or just cleaned
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the wash 这一说法，指待洗或刚洗好的衣物
senses.example: Her wet socks were still in the wash.
senses.exampleCN: 她湿掉的袜子还泡在待洗的衣物里。
senses.why: A concrete pile grows out of the abstract act: what is being washed becomes the wash itself.
senses.whyCN: 具体的一堆东西从抽象动作里长出来：正在被洗的东西本身就叫 the wash。

intro.en: Wash is an Old English verb, and nearly every Germanic language has a cousin of it.
intro.cn: wash 是古英语动词，几乎每种日耳曼语都有它的近亲。

items.en: Wascan meant 'to wash, to cleanse with water'; the noun wæsc meant a washing.
items.cn: wascan 意为「用水洗、洗净」，名词 wæsc 指一次洗涤。

items.en: German waschen and Dutch wassen are exact cognates of the same root.
items.cn: 德语 waschen 与荷兰语 wassen 是同一词根的精确同源词。

items.en: The root is related to words for water in older European languages; the exact reconstruction is debated.
items.cn: 这个词根与更古老欧洲语言中的「水」类词有关，确切重构仍有争议。

items.en: Wasshen kept both the cleaning sense and the sense of water sweeping things along.
items.cn: 中古英语 wasshen 既保留洗涤义，也保留水流冲走东西之义。

items.en: Machines gave the word new nouns: the washing, the washer, the wash cycle.
items.cn: 机器给了这个词新的名词：the washing、the washer、wash cycle。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the wash shape; the near-meaning group gathers ways of cleaning.
note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的 wash 类词；近义组收各种清洁的说法。

entries.definition: The activity of washing, or the clothes being washed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「洗涤」或「待洗的衣物」。

entries.definition: A washing machine, or the flat ring that seals a joint.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「洗衣机」，或指密封用的垫圈。

entries.definition: Able to be washed without damage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可水洗的」。

entries.definition: To look at steadily; a different word, close in sound only.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「观看」，只是发音相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: To clean with clean water only, without soap.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「冲洗」，只用水不用肥皂。

entries.definition: To remove dirt in any way; broader than wash.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「清洁」，方式不限，范围比 wash 宽。

entries.definition: To wash a whole body in a bath or the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「沐浴」，指整体泡洗。

entries.definition: To rub hard with a brush; more force than wash.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「刷洗」，比 wash 用力得多。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wascan and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wascan，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Water plus friction: that is the whole of wash.
normal.cn: 水加上摩擦：wash 的全部含义就在这里。

normal.en: Wash your hands, wash the dishes, wash the car: the object changes, the action does not.
normal.cn: 洗手、洗碗、洗车：对象在变，动作不变。

normal.en: Wash away means the water takes it off; wash off means you remove it.
normal.cn: wash away 是水把它带走，wash off 是你把它去掉。

normal.en: The wash is not the act but the pile of clothes waiting.
normal.cn: the wash 不是动作，而是等着洗的那堆衣服。

normal.en: Washing machine, dish washer, washroom: machines borrowed the old verb.
normal.cn: washing machine、dish washer、washroom：机器借用了这个古老动词。

abstract.en: Picture dirt loosened by water and carried off: the word always has something leaving.
abstract.cn: 想象脏东西被水泡松、被带走：这个词永远有个东西正在离开。

abstract.en: The same verb serves skin, dishes, clothes and even bridges, because water behaves the same way everywhere.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词适用于皮肤、碗碟、衣物甚至桥梁，因为水在各处都一样作为。

abstract.en: Cleaning and carrying away are one motion seen from two ends: what leaves the cup is what cleans it.
abstract.cn: 清洁与带走是同一动作的两端：离开杯子的东西正是清洗它的东西。

examples.en: Wash the vegetables under cold running water.
examples.cn: 在冷流水下冲洗蔬菜。

examples.en: The storm washed the soil off the hillside.
examples.cn: 暴雨把山坡上的泥土冲走了。

examples.en: There is a big wash waiting on Sunday morning.
examples.cn: 星期天早上有一大堆衣服等着洗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我洗」——wash 听起来就像「我洗」：洗

root: 古英语 wascan「洗、洗净」，源自日耳曼语同一词根，与德语 waschen、荷兰语 wassen 同源；派生词有 washing、washer、washable。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of wash follow water at work: cleaning a thing, cleaning the body, carrying something away, the act itself, and finally the pile of clothes.
sensesIntro.cn: wash 的五个义项跟着水在工作：洗净物件、清洗身体、把东西带走、动作本身，最后是那堆衣服。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basin of water stirred, dirt lifted off, a clean surface underneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盆水被搅动，脏物离开，露出底下干净的一层。

branches.en: CLEANING LINE: objects and bodies come out clean.
branches.cn: 清洁线：物件与身体被洗得干净。

branches.en: FORCE LINE: water without soap simply takes things away.
branches.cn: 冲力线：没有肥皂的水只是把东西带走。

branches.en: ACT LINE: one wash counted as one occasion.
branches.cn: 动作线：一次洗算作一次。

branches.en: OBJECT LINE: the clothes themselves become the wash.
branches.cn: 物件线：衣服本身成了 the wash。

branches.en: CONTRAST: rinse is water only, scrub is force, clean is any way.
branches.cn: 对照线：rinse 只用水，scrub 靠力，clean 方式不限。

intro.en: Wash is a native verb, and its derivatives are built with ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: wash 是本族动词，其派生词都由普通英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 浪费；废物、垃圾；浪费的时间或金钱；动词：浪费、滥用；荒废的
definition_en: to use something carelessly so that it is lost, or material that is thrown away because it is no longer wanted
core_image: 水从没关紧的龙头里一直滴，地上积成一片没人要的湿痕
scene: 食堂收餐口的桶里堆着大半个没吃完的饭盒。So much food is wasted every day that the kitchen began weighing it.
sceneCN: 这里 waste 是「浪费」（第 4 个义项：不加珍惜地用掉，使之白白失去）；句意为每天浪费的食物太多，厨房开始称重。水白白流走、饭被倒掉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：浪费、滥用；错过
名词：废物、垃圾；浪费；荒地
形容词：废弃的；荒芜的

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ful 构成，义为「浪费的；不节俭的」
加后缀 -age 构成，义为「损耗；浪费量」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「浪费者；废品」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「被浪费的；憔悴的」

senses.title: A desert or empty land
senses.titleCN: 荒地：无人居住的空旷之地
senses.definition: a large area of land that is empty, wild and not used for farming
senses.definitionCN: 大片空旷、野生、不用于耕种的土地
senses.example: Beyond the last field lies a wide waste of stone and thorn.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一块田之外，是一片石头与荆棘的荒地。
senses.why: Old French wast meant empty and desolate, and English kept that picture of land with nothing on it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 wast 意为「空的、荒凉的」，英语保留了那片空无一物的土地的画面。

senses.title: To destroy and leave empty
senses.titleCN: 使荒芜：毁坏而使之空无
senses.definition: to damage a place so badly that it is left empty or ruined
senses.definitionCN: 把某地毁坏到空无或残破的地步
senses.example: The long war wasted the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的战争让整个山谷变得荒芜。
senses.why: The adjective of emptiness becomes an action: to make a place into a waste.
senses.whyCN: 表示「空」的形容词变成动作：把某地变成一片荒地。

senses.title: Rubbish and unwanted material
senses.titleCN: 废物、垃圾：不再需要而被丢弃的东西
senses.definition: material that is no longer wanted and is thrown away
senses.definitionCN: 已不需要、被丢弃的物质
senses.example: The factory must treat its waste before it enters the river.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂必须先把废物处理掉，才能排入河中。
senses.why: What is left after use is like a wasteland: nothing grows on it, so it is set aside.
senses.whyCN: 用剩下的东西就像荒地：上面长不出什么，只好被弃置一旁。

senses.title: To use carelessly
senses.titleCN: 浪费：不加珍惜地用掉
senses.definition: to use money, time or effort badly, so that it brings no benefit
senses.definitionCN: 不善加利用金钱、时间或精力，使之无所收益
senses.example: Do not waste hot water on a small load of dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 别为几个碗浪费热水。
senses.why: Spending what could have been used well turns a resource into waste; the verb names that turning.
senses.whyCN: 把本可好好利用的东西花掉，资源就变成了废物；动词命名的正是这一转变。

senses.title: As in wasted effort or a wasted chance
senses.titleCN: 白白错过：努力或机会被耗掉
senses.definition: used of effort, opportunity or a person's condition when something valuable comes to nothing
senses.definitionCN: 用于努力、机会或人的状态，指宝贵的东西最终落空
senses.example: All their careful planning was wasted when the road was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 路一封闭，他们所有的精心安排都白费了。
senses.why: The lost value is no longer money but possibility: what might have happened now cannot.
senses.whyCN: 失去的不再是钱，而是可能性：本可能发生的事如今不可能了。

intro.en: Waste came from Latin vastus through Old French, and its first meaning was empty land.
intro.cn: waste 经古法语来自拉丁语 vastus，最初的意思是空旷的土地。

items.en: Vastus meant 'empty, desolate, huge'; the emptiness came before the size in English use.
items.cn: vastus 意为「空的、荒凉的、巨大的」；在英语用法中，空义先于大义。

items.en: The verb vastare meant 'to lay waste, to devastate', turning emptiness into an action.
items.cn: 动词 vastare 意为「使荒芜、毁坏」，把「空」变成了动作。

items.en: Old French had both gast and waste, meaning 'empty, ruined' and 'a waste place'.
items.cn: 古法语有 gast 与 waste 两种形式，意为「空的、毁坏的」与「荒地」。

items.en: English took waste as noun, adjective and verb together in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪同时把 waste 用作名词、形容词和动词。

items.en: Industry added the rubbish sense: household waste, waste paper, waste water.
items.cn: 工业补充了垃圾义：生活垃圾、废纸、废水。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same empty-root family; the near-meaning group gathers ways of squandering and of rubbish.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「空」词根词族；近义组收挥霍与垃圾类说法。

entries.definition: Extremely large; the same Latin vastus, with the size sense only.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「辽阔的」，同出拉丁语 vastus，只保留「大」义。

entries.definition: To destroy a place completely; Latin de- plus vastare.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毁坏」，由 de- 加 vastare 构成。

entries.definition: Using more than is needed; the adjective of the squandering sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「浪费的」，是挥霍义的形容词形式。

entries.definition: Land that is empty and cannot be farmed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒地」，即空旷无法耕种之地。

entries.definition: To spend money or time foolishly; stronger and more disapproving.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挥霍」，语气更强、更带责备。

entries.definition: Unwanted things; the British everyday word for waste.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾」，是英式日常说法。

entries.definition: Waste food and household rubbish; the American everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「垃圾」，尤指厨余，是美式日常说法。

entries.definition: To give or use without harming oneself; the opposite of wasting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「腾出、剩下」，与浪费相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin vastus and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 vastus，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: waste and vast share a root: empty land, and land just very big.
normal.cn: waste 与 vast 同根：一片是空地，一片只是很大。

normal.en: To waste is to turn a resource into rubbish.
normal.cn: waste 就是把资源变成垃圾。

normal.en: A waste of time costs more than a waste of paper.
normal.cn: 浪费时间的代价比浪费纸张大得多。

normal.en: Household waste is what leaves the house to be thrown away.
normal.cn: household waste 就是被运出家门的垃圾。

normal.en: Lay waste to a place and it becomes a waste: the verb and the noun meet.
normal.cn: lay waste to 一个地方，它就变成一片 waste：动词与名词在此相遇。

abstract.en: Picture a tap left dripping overnight: the water is not dirty, only lost.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水龙头一夜没关紧：水并不脏，只是白白流掉了。

abstract.en: The two halves of the word meet at the same point: what is thrown away is what was never used well.
abstract.cn: 这个词的两半在同一点相遇：被丢弃的，正是从未被好好利用的。

abstract.en: Emptiness is the hinge: a wasted field, a wasted chance and a waste bin all hold nothing useful.
abstract.cn: 空是那个铰链：荒掉的地、白费的机会、垃圾箱，都装着没用的东西。

examples.en: He wasted two hours waiting for a bus that never came.
examples.cn: 他白等了两个小时，那趟公交始终没来。

examples.en: The city collects household waste every Tuesday.
examples.cn: 这座城市每周二收集生活垃圾。

examples.en: It is a waste of money to buy a new one when this still works.
examples.cn: 这个还能用，再买个新的纯属浪费钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂（wei）死它（ste）」——把好东西喂给垃圾桶，活活浪费：浪费

root: 源自拉丁语 vastus「空的、荒凉的」，动词 vastare「使荒芜」，经古法语 waste 进入英语；同族词有 vast、devastate。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of waste start from empty land, move to the act of emptying a place, then to rubbish, to squandering, and finally to any chance that comes to nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: waste 的五个义项从荒地开始，到把地方弄空的动作，再到垃圾、挥霍，最后是一切落空的机会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tap left dripping overnight, the water lost without ever being dirty.
core.cn: 核心意象：一夜没关紧的水龙头，水并不脏，却全部流失。

branches.en: LAND LINE: empty ground, and the act of making it empty.
branches.cn: 土地线：空旷的地，以及把它弄空的动作。

branches.en: RUBBISH LINE: what use leaves behind is thrown away.
branches.cn: 垃圾线：使用之后剩下的被丢弃。

branches.en: SQUANDER LINE: resources used so badly they become rubbish.
branches.cn: 挥霍线：资源被用得极糟，于是成了垃圾。

branches.en: CHANCE LINE: the lost thing is now possibility, not money.
branches.cn: 机会线：失去的已是可能性而非金钱。

branches.en: CONTRAST: spare keeps something; waste loses it.
branches.cn: 对照线：spare 留下东西，waste 让它失去。

intro.en: Waste is a Latin adjective and verb that English turned into three word classes at once.
intro.cn: waste 本是拉丁语的形容词与动词，英语把它一次性用成了三种词类。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vastus and vastare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：vastus 与 vastare。

definition_zh: 虚弱；弱点、缺陷；（对某事物的）偏爱、迷恋
definition_en: lack of strength, a fault in a person or thing, or a strong liking that is hard to resist
core_image: 一根细绳被拉得发紧，中间已经有了磨白的痕迹
scene: 老木桥的栏杆被人一靠就晃，木板缝里透出下面的河。The weakness of the old bridge was obvious to anyone who looked closely.
sceneCN: 这里 weakness 是「弱点、缺陷」（第 2 个义项：人或事物不够牢固的地方）；句意为任何人只要看仔细些，都能发现这座老桥的弱点。磨白的绳痕，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：虚弱、无力；弱点、缺陷；偏爱

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根形容词，义为「虚弱的；薄弱的」
加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「削弱；变弱」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「虚弱地；无力地」
由 weak 加 -ing 构成，义为「体弱者」（口语罕用）

senses.title: Lack of physical strength
senses.titleCN: 虚弱：身体力气不足
senses.definition: the state of lacking physical strength or energy
senses.definitionCN: 缺少体力或精力的状态
senses.example: After the fever, a deep weakness stayed in his legs for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 退烧之后，他双腿的虚弱感持续了好几周。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns an adjective into a state; weakness is simply the state of being weak.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ness 把形容词变成状态；weakness 就是「弱」这一状态。

senses.title: A fault in a person
senses.titleCN: 弱点：性格上的不足
senses.definition: a fault or defect in someone's character, such as impatience or pride
senses.definitionCN: 某人性格中的欠缺，如急躁或自负
senses.example: His one real weakness is that he cannot say no to a friend.
senses.exampleCN: 他唯一真正的弱点是无法拒绝朋友的请求。
senses.why: The adjective weak names a lack of strength; -ness turns that lack into a countable fault, one particular place where the strength runs out.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 weak 表示力量不足；后缀 -ness 把这种不足变成可数的缺点，即力量耗尽的某一处。

senses.title: A weak point in a thing
senses.titleCN: 缺陷：事物中不牢固的地方
senses.definition: a part of a system, structure or argument that is not strong or convincing
senses.definitionCN: 系统、结构或论证中不够牢固、不够有说服力的部分
senses.example: Engineers found a weakness where the two beams meet.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师发现两根梁相接之处的薄弱点。
senses.why: The same noun moves from people to things: any structure is judged by its least strong part.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从人移到物：任何结构都以最不牢固的部分来评判。

senses.title: A strong liking
senses.titleCN: 偏爱：难以抗拒的迷恋
senses.definition: a strong liking for something that one finds hard to resist
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物强烈而难以抗拒的喜爱
senses.example: She has a weakness for old watches.
senses.exampleCN: 她对旧手表有一种偏爱。
senses.why: Here the fault turns inward and pleasant: a liking you cannot resist is a weak spot in your self-control.
senses.whyCN: 这里缺陷转向内里且变得愉快：抵挡不住的喜爱，正是自制力上的薄弱处。

senses.title: Lack of force or authority
senses.titleCN: 软弱无力：力量或权威不足
senses.definition: lack of strength in a government, argument or action, so that it has little effect
senses.definitionCN: 政府、论证或行动缺乏力度，因而收效甚微
senses.example: The weakness of the new law was clear from the first month.
