senses.exampleCN: 新法的软弱无力在头一个月就显露出来。
senses.why: Weakness of a law or a case means it cannot stand up to challenge, the same image of strength running out.
senses.whyCN: 法律或论证的软弱，指它经不起挑战，仍是力量耗尽的同一意象。

intro.en: Weakness is a native English compound of the old adjective weak and the noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: weakness 是本族英语复合词，由古老形容词 weak 与名词后缀 -ness 组成。

items.en: The adjective veikr meant 'pliant, weak'; it entered English from Norse rather than from Old English.
items.cn: 形容词 veikr 意为「柔软的、弱的」，是从古诺尔斯语而非古英语进入英语的。

items.en: Old English had its own wac, meaning 'weak, pliant', related to the verb wican 'to give way'.
items.cn: 古英语自有 wac，意为「弱的、柔软的」，与动词 wican「退让」相关。

items.en: The two forms merged into the single adjective weik or weak in the north of England first.
items.cn: 两种形式合并为单一形容词，先在英格兰北部写成 weik 或 weak。

items.en: The suffix -nesse was fully productive, so weakness appeared as soon as the adjective was established.
items.cn: 后缀 -nesse 当时构词能力很强，形容词一成形，weakness 便随之出现。

items.en: The figurative senses, a fault and a fondness, are later extensions of the same state.
items.cn: 「缺陷」与「迷恋」两个比喻义，是同一种状态后来伸出的延伸。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the weak family; the near-meaning group gathers words for faults and for fondness.
note.cn: 形近组收 weak 一族词；近义组收表示缺陷与偏爱的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for lacking strength; the base of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「虚弱的」，是名词的词根。

entries.definition: To make or become weaker.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「削弱；变弱」。

entries.definition: In a weak way; also an old adjective meaning sickly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「虚弱地」；也曾是表示「病弱的」形容词。

entries.definition: Seven days; a homophone with no connection in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「星期」，与本词同音，来源无关。

entries.definition: A small fault that spoils something; sharper and more specific.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「瑕疵、缺陷」，更尖锐也更具体。

entries.definition: A mistake or a defect for which someone can be blamed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「过错、缺点」，含可归咎之意。

entries.definition: Weakness of body or character, especially in old age.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脆弱」，多指年老体弱或性格弱点。

entries.definition: A minor weakness in a person's character.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺点」，多指性格上的小毛病。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old Norse veikr and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古诺尔斯语 veikr，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: weak plus -ness: the suffix simply names the state, so weakness is the state of being weak.
normal.cn: weak 加 -ness：后缀只是给状态命名，weakness 就是「弱」的状态。

normal.en: Strengths and weaknesses always come in pairs: an honest list has both.
normal.cn: 长处与短处总是成对出现：诚实的清单上两样都有。

normal.en: A weakness for chocolate is not a defect but a fondness.
normal.cn: a weakness for chocolate 不是缺陷，而是一种偏爱。

normal.en: Weakness in an argument is a gap where evidence should be.
normal.cn: 论证中的 weakness 就是本该有证据的空缺。

normal.en: Week is a homophone and means seven days; weakness means no strength.
normal.cn: week 同音，指七天；weakness 指没有力气。

abstract.en: Picture a rope worn pale in the middle: the weak point is where the strain shows first.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子中间磨得发白：弱点就是拉力最先显形的地方。

abstract.en: The word works for bodies, buildings, arguments and hearts, because all can give way under pressure.
abstract.cn: 这个词适用于身体、建筑、论证和人心，因为它们在压力下都可能让步。

abstract.en: Finding a weakness is not an insult; it is where a repair or a defence belongs.
abstract.cn: 找到弱点并不是侮辱，那正是修补或防守该落脚的地方。

examples.en: Weakness in the knees made the climb dangerous.
examples.cn: 膝盖无力让这次攀登变得危险。

examples.en: Every plan has a weakness, and this one is the budget.
examples.cn: 每个计划都有薄弱处，这个计划的薄弱处就是预算。

examples.en: He has a weakness for cheap second-hand books.
examples.cn: 他对便宜的二手书有种偏爱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「唯一（wei）克（k）尼斯（ness）」——唯一被克制的尼斯湖怪，因为太虚弱：虚弱

root: 由古诺尔斯语 veikr「柔软的、弱的」与古英语 wac 合流而成的 weak，加名词后缀 -ness 构成；同族词有 weaken、weakly、weakling。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weakness begin with the plain state of no strength, then name a fault in a person, a gap in a thing, a fondness, and a general lack of force.
sensesIntro.cn: weakness 的五个义项始于「没有力气」这一朴素状态，继而指人的缺点、事物的空隙、一种偏爱，以及普遍的力量不足。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope worn pale in the middle where the strain shows first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根中间磨得发白的绳子，拉力最先在那里显形。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the muscles have no force left.
branches.cn: 身体线：肌肉再也使不出力。

branches.en: CHARACTER LINE: a person cannot resist a certain impulse.
branches.cn: 性格线：人抗拒不了某种冲动。

branches.en: STRUCTURE LINE: a beam, a law or an argument lacks force.
branches.cn: 结构线：梁、法条或论证缺乏力度。

branches.en: DESIRE LINE: the same word turns kind, naming a fondness.
branches.cn: 欲望线：同一个词转得温柔，指一种偏爱。

branches.en: CONTRAST: flaw is sharper, failing is gentler, weakness is the plainest.
branches.cn: 对照线：flaw 更尖锐，failing 更温和，weakness 最朴素。

intro.en: Weakness is a Germanic adjective plus the native -ness suffix; no Latin element is involved.
intro.cn: weakness 是日耳曼语形容词加本族的 -ness 后缀，不涉及拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.example: It merged with the Norse form.
items.exampleCN: 它与诺尔斯语形式合流。

items.example: It is the old verb behind wac.
items.exampleCN: 它是 wac 背后的古老动词。

definition_zh: 富有的；富裕的；丰富的
definition_en: having a large amount of money and possessions, or having plenty of something valuable
core_image: 一间储满粮食与布匹的库房，门一开就能看出屋主的家底
scene: 村口的宅子有石墙和两层楼，院子里停着两辆车。The town grew wealthy on the wool trade in the sixteenth century.
sceneCN: 这里 wealthy 是「富有的」（第 1 个义项：拥有大量钱财与产业）；句意为这座城镇在十六世纪靠羊毛贸易富了起来。库房里堆满的粮食与布匹，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：富有的；富裕的；丰富的、大量的

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根名词，义为「财富；大量」
加副词后缀构成，义为「富足地；阔气地」
加名词后缀构成，义为「富裕」
与 well 相关的形近词，义为「福祉；幸福」

senses.title: Having much money
senses.titleCN: 富有的：拥有大量钱财与产业
senses.definition: having a great deal of money, property or other material goods
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量金钱、产业或其他物质财富
senses.example: The wealthy merchant owned four ships and half the dock.
senses.exampleCN: 这位富商拥有四条船和半个码头。
senses.why: Old English weal means well-being, and wealth was originally that whole state; money became its measure.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 weal 意为「安好」，wealth 本指整个好境况；金钱后来成了它的度量。

senses.title: As a group
senses.titleCN: 富人：作为一个群体来看的富有者
senses.definition: in the phrase the wealthy, the whole group of rich people
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the wealthy，指全部富人这一群体
senses.example: The tax falls hardest on the wealthy and lightest on the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税对富人最重，对穷人最轻。
senses.why: Adjectives preceded by the can name a class, so the rich quality turns into the people who have it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词前加 the 可以指一类人，于是「富」这一性质变成了拥有它的人群。

senses.title: Rich in natural goods
senses.titleCN: 资源丰富的：物产或条件富足
senses.definition: rich in natural resources, land or production
senses.definitionCN: 在自然资源、土地或产出方面富足
senses.example: The valley is wealthy in water, which the plains below lack.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷水源丰富，而下面的平原却缺水。
senses.why: The abundance that money measures also exists in land: the word follows the goods, not the bank account.
senses.whyCN: 金钱所衡量的那种充足也存在于土地中：这个词跟的是物产，而不是银行户头。

senses.title: Rich in a quality
senses.titleCN: 丰富的：在某种特质上含量多
senses.definition: having a large amount of a particular quality or element, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某种品质或成分含量很多
senses.example: The region is wealthy in stories, and every village tells them differently.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带故事极多，每个村庄讲得都不一样。
senses.why: Once plenty is the meaning, anything countable can be the treasure that fills the storehouse.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「充足」成了核心义，任何可数的东西都能成为填满库房的宝藏。

senses.title: Prosperous in life
senses.titleCN: 富足的：生活宽裕的
senses.definition: enjoying a comfortable and prosperous way of life, without the stress on huge sums
senses.definitionCN: 生活舒适宽裕，不特别强调数目巨大
senses.example: After two good harvests the farmhouse looked wealthy again.
senses.exampleCN: 连收两季好庄稼之后，那座农舍又显得富足了。
senses.why: This is the old well-being again, visible in a house rather than counted in coins.
senses.whyCN: 这又回到了古老的「安好」，它显在一座房子里，而不是数在铜板中。

intro.en: Wealthy grows from wealth, whose oldest sense was not money but well-being.
intro.cn: wealthy 由 wealth 生长而来，而 wealth 最初的意思不是钱，而是「安好」。

items.en: Weal meant 'well-being, welfare, prosperity', the same element as in commonweal.
items.cn: weal 意为「安好、福祉、兴旺」，与 commonweal 中的成分相同。

items.en: Wela meant 'wealth, riches', and the two words were closely associated.
items.cn: wela 意为「财富、财宝」，两者关系密切。

items.en: Wele or welthe came to name both prosperity and the things that show it.
items.cn: 中古英语 wele 与 welthe 既指兴旺，也指显出兴旺的那些东西。

items.en: The suffix -y forms the adjective, and wealthy appears alongside the older wele. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 构成形容词 wealthy，它与更早的 wele 并存；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense narrowed toward money and property, while the figurative sense of abundance survived.
items.cn: 词义向金钱与财产收窄，而表示「丰富」的比喻义照旧留存。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wealth family; the near-meaning group gathers words for being rich.
note.cn: 形近组收 wealth 一族词；近义组收表示富有的词。

entries.definition: Riches, or a large amount of something good.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财富」，或指某物的「大量」。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for the state of being wealthy; rare in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「富裕」，口语中罕见。

entries.definition: The state of being well in body; a shared shape, different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「健康」，与 wealthy 形近而义不同。

entries.definition: A political community; keeps the old weal of well-being.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「联邦、共同体」，保留了 weal「福祉」的旧义。

entries.definition: Having much money or many resources; the commonest word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富的」，是最常用的说法。

entries.definition: Prosperous and well-off; formal and often about societies.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富裕的」，语气正式，多用于社会群体。

entries.definition: Comfortably provided for, without implying great riches.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽裕的」，不含巨富之意。

entries.definition: Thriving and successful, often of a business or a town.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「兴旺的」，多形容事业或城镇。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English weal and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 weal，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: wealth began as well-being, and only later counted money.
normal.cn: wealth 起初指安好，后来才开始数钱。

normal.en: Wealthy adds -y to wealth, just as healthy adds -y to health.
normal.cn: wealthy 由 wealth 加 -y，正如 healthy 由 health 加 -y。

normal.en: The wealthy means all rich people together, not one rich person.
normal.cn: the wealthy 指全部富人，不是某一位富人。

normal.en: A region can be wealthy in water or in stories, not only in cash.
normal.cn: 一个地区可以水富、故事富，不只是钱富。

normal.en: Well-off is milder than wealthy; it stops short of great riches.
normal.cn: well-off 比 wealthy 温和，不含巨富之意。

abstract.en: Picture a storehouse packed with grain and cloth: the wealth shows in what can be drawn on.
abstract.cn: 想象一间堆满粮食与布匹的库房：财富显现在可取用的东西上。

abstract.en: The word measures plenty, so it can point at money, water, or a store of tales.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量的是「充足」，所以能指向金钱、水，或一大堆故事。

abstract.en: Its oldest layer is not greed but welfare: to be wealthy once meant to be well.
abstract.cn: 它最古老的一层不是贪婪而是福祉：有钱曾经意味着过得好。

examples.en: The wealthy family owned most of the land in the valley.
examples.cn: 那个富裕家族拥有谷中大部分土地。

examples.en: The country is wealthy in forests but poor in oil.
examples.cn: 这个国家森林丰富，却缺乏石油。

examples.en: The shop moved to a wealthier district last spring.
examples.cn: 这家店去年春天搬到了更富裕的街区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威（weal）尔西（thy）」——威尔西家库房里粮布堆到屋顶：富有的

root: 由中古英语 welthe「兴旺、财富」加形容词后缀 -y 构成，更早来自古英语 weal「福祉」与 wela「财富」；同族词有 wealth、commonwealth。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of wealthy run from cash and property to the class of rich people, then to abundance of resources, of qualities, and of a comfortable life.
sensesIntro.cn: wealthy 的五个义项从钱财产业出发，到富人这一群体，再到资源充足、品质丰富，以及生活宽裕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a storehouse packed with grain and cloth, its wealth plain as soon as the door opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间堆满粮食布匹的库房，门一开就看得出家底。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: cash, property and a comfortable life.
branches.cn: 金钱线：现金、产业与宽裕的生活。

branches.en: CLASS LINE: the adjective becomes a name for rich people.
branches.cn: 群体线：形容词成了富人的称呼。

branches.en: PLENTY LINE: water, forests or stories in abundance.
branches.cn: 充足线：水、森林或故事方面的丰富。

branches.en: ROOT LINE: the old sense of well-being still glows under the money.
branches.cn: 词根线：金钱之下还隐约闪着古老的「安好」义。

branches.en: CONTRAST: rich is plainer, affluent more formal.
branches.cn: 对照线：rich 更朴素，affluent 更正式。

intro.en: Wealthy is a native noun plus the common adjective suffix -y.
intro.cn: wealthy 是本族名词加常见形容词后缀 -y 构成的。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 穿、戴；磨损、穿旧；耐穿；名词：磨损；衣着
definition_en: to have clothes on the body, to damage something by long use, or the damage caused by use
core_image: 一件外套的袖口被日日挽起，布料薄了、起了毛
scene: 冬天的早晨，她在门口匆匆披上大衣，围巾绕了两圈。He wore the same grey coat all winter and never complained.
sceneCN: 这里 wear 是「穿、戴」（第 1 个义项：把衣物穿在身上）；句意为他整个冬天都穿同一件灰大衣，从不抱怨。被日日穿戴而磨损的袖口，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：穿、戴；磨损、用旧；耐用
名词：磨损；衣着（多用于复合词）

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「磨破的；疲惫的」
加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「令人疲惫的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「穿戴者」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可穿戴的（含电子设备）」

senses.title: To have clothes on
senses.titleCN: 穿、戴：把衣物首饰带在身上
senses.definition: to have clothes, shoes, glasses or jewellery on the body
senses.definitionCN: 把衣服、鞋、眼镜或首饰带在身上
senses.example: She wears glasses only when she reads.
senses.exampleCN: 她只在看书时戴眼镜。
senses.why: Old English werian meant to have on the body; the idea is carrying something on yourself, not putting it away.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 werian 意为「穿在身上」；这一观念是把东西带在身上，而不是收起来。

senses.title: To have a look or expression
senses.titleCN: 面带：带着某种神情或气色
senses.definition: to have a particular expression or appearance on the face
senses.definitionCN: 脸上带着某种表情或样子
senses.example: He wore a tired smile all through the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 整场会议他都带着疲惫的笑。
senses.why: The face is treated like clothing: an expression can be put on and carried about.
senses.whyCN: 脸被当作衣物来对待：表情也能穿上身，带着走来走去。

senses.title: To damage by use
senses.titleCN: 磨损：长期使用而变薄变坏
senses.definition: to damage or make thin by long or repeated use
senses.definitionCN: 因长期或反复使用而磨损、变薄
senses.example: The stairs were worn hollow in the middle.
senses.exampleCN: 那段楼梯中间被踏得凹了下去。
senses.why: Use rubs away material; the same verb now describes what the wearing does to the thing.
senses.whyCN: 使用会磨去材质；同一个动词此时描述这种穿戴对东西做了什么。

senses.title: To last in use
senses.titleCN: 耐用：经得起长期使用
senses.definition: to remain in good condition after much use, used of materials and products
senses.definitionCN: 指材料与产品经久使用仍完好
senses.example: Good leather shoes wear well for years.
senses.exampleCN: 好皮鞋能穿好多年。
senses.why: The same process is viewed from the object's side: either it rubs away or it holds.
senses.whyCN: 同一过程从物体这一侧看：它或磨掉，或撑住。

senses.title: The damage itself
senses.titleCN: 磨损：被磨出的耗损
senses.definition: the damage or loss of material caused by use
senses.definitionCN: 因使用造成的材质损耗
senses.example: Check the tyres for wear before the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途驾驶前检查轮胎的磨损。
senses.why: The action becomes a noun, and the noun names the mark left behind.
senses.whyCN: 动作化为名词，而名词指留下的痕迹。

intro.en: Wear is an Old English verb meaning to carry on the body, and it has always had both the clothing and the rubbing sense.
intro.cn: wear 是古英语动词，意为「在身上带着」，一直兼具穿戴与摩擦两个意思。

items.en: Werian meant 'to wear, to have on the body', and also 'to defend' in an older layer.
items.cn: werian 意为「穿、把……带在身上」，更早一层还有「防护」之义。

items.en: The past forms wore and worn keep an old vowel pattern shared with bear and swear.
items.cn: 过去式 wore 与过去分词 worn 保留了与 bear、swear 共有的古老元音模式。

items.en: A separate verb, often written werian as well, meant to weary or tire, and the 'wear out' sense grew partly from it.
items.cn: 另一个动词（也常写作 werian）意为使疲乏，wear out 的「耗尽」义部分源自它。

items.en: The clothing and the rubbing senses were already side by side, as they are today.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，穿戴义与磨损义已经并列，一如今天。

items.en: New compounds keep arriving: footwear, sportswear, wearable devices.
items.cn: 新的复合词不断出现：footwear、sportswear、wearable devices。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wear family; the near-meaning group gathers dressing and damaging words.
note.cn: 形近组收 wear 一族词；近义组收穿衣与磨损类词。

entries.definition: Damaged by use, or very tired; the past participle as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「磨破的、疲惫的」，是过去分词转来的形容词。

entries.definition: Tiring to do or to be with.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人疲惫的」。

entries.definition: The person who has something on.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「穿戴者」。

entries.definition: The question word for place; a homophone trap.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在哪里」，与 wear 同音，易混。

entries.definition: To put clothes on; more about the act than about having them on.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「穿衣」，侧重穿衣动作。

entries.definition: To place clothes on the body at one moment; wear is the resulting state.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「穿上」，指某一刻的动作，而 wear 是穿着的状态。

entries.definition: To wear away slowly by natural forces such as water or wind.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「侵蚀」，多指自然力缓慢磨去。

entries.definition: Of cloth, to become worn into loose threads.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「磨散」，多指布料磨出线头。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English werian and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 werian，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Put on is the moment; wear is the day that follows.
normal.cn: put on 是那一刻；wear 是之后的一整天。

normal.en: Wear out means both used up and tired out.
normal.cn: wear out 既指磨坏，也指累垮。

normal.en: Wear off is for a feeling or a mark slowly leaving.
normal.cn: wear off 指感觉或痕迹慢慢消失。

normal.en: When patience wears thin, the same cloth image is at work.
normal.cn: 耐心 wearable thin 时，用的还是同一块布的形象。

normal.en: Wore and worn follow the pattern of bore, borne and tore, torn.
normal.cn: wore 与 worn 遵循 bore、borne、tore、torn 的模式。

abstract.en: Picture a coat cuff rolled up every morning: the cloth thins exactly where the habit happens.
abstract.cn: 想象每天早晨都挽起的袖口：布料正是在习惯发生的地方变薄。

abstract.en: Clothing and erosion are one word because both are things carried and rubbed by daily life.
abstract.cn: 穿衣与磨损是同一个词，因为两者都是被日常生活带着、磨着的东西。

abstract.en: A face can wear a smile for the same reason a body wears a coat: both are put on for others to see.
abstract.cn: 脸可以带着笑，正如身体穿着外套：两样都是穿给旁人看的。

examples.en: He wore a dark suit to the interview.
examples.cn: 他穿了深色西装去面试。

examples.en: The carpet has worn thin near the door.
examples.cn: 门口那块地毯已经磨薄了。

examples.en: This jacket has worn well for six winters.
examples.cn: 这件夹克已经穿了六个冬天，依然耐穿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂（wea）儿（r）」——每天喂孩子穿衣，衣服慢慢被穿旧：穿；磨损

root: 古英语 werian「穿、带在身上」，源自日耳曼语同一词根；过去式 wore、过去分词 worn 保留古老元音变换；同族词有 worn、wearer、wearable。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of wear run from clothes on the body, to a look worn on the face, to material rubbed away, to a thing that lasts, and finally to the damage itself.
sensesIntro.cn: wear 的五个义项从身上的衣物，到脸上的神情，到被磨去的材质，到经得起使用，最后是磨损本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat cuff rolled up each morning, the cloth gone thin where the habit falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天早晨挽起的袖口，习惯落处布料变薄。

branches.en: BODY LINE: clothes and expressions are both carried on us.
branches.cn: 身体线：衣物与神情都是带在身上的。

branches.en: EROSION LINE: use rubs the material away.
branches.cn: 侵蚀线：使用把材质磨去。

branches.en: DURABILITY LINE: the same rubbing seen from the object's side.
branches.cn: 耐用线：同一摩擦从物体一侧来看。

branches.en: RESULT LINE: the noun names the mark left by use.
branches.cn: 结果线：名词指使用留下的痕迹。

branches.en: CONTRAST: put on is a moment, wear is a state.
branches.cn: 对照线：put on 是瞬间，wear 是状态。

intro.en: Wear is a strong native verb; its derivatives use plain English endings.
intro.cn: wear 是本族的强变化动词，其派生词使用普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 网站；网页集合；（一个域下的）站点
definition_en: a set of connected pages on the internet, usually belonging to one person or organisation
core_image: 一张网把许多房间连起来，每个房间门口挂着一块招牌
scene: 小书店的柜台旁贴着二维码，顾客扫开就能看到全部书目。The bookshop's website lists every title it has in stock.
sceneCN: 这里 website 是「网站」（第 1 个义项：互联网上相互连接的一系列页面）；句意为这家书店的网站列出了所有库存书目。门上挂招牌的连片房间，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：网站；站点

derivatives.zh: 截短形式，义为「站点；场地」
复合词，义为「网页」
复合词，义为「网站管理员」
本词的第一部分，义为「网；万维网」

senses.title: A set of connected pages
senses.titleCN: 网站：互相链接的一组页面
senses.definition: a group of connected pages on the internet that share one address
senses.definitionCN: 互联网上共用同一地址、彼此相连的一组页面
senses.example: The museum's website has a virtual tour of every hall.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的网站上有每个展厅的虚拟导览。
senses.why: web names the linking and site names the place; a website is a place built out of links.
senses.whyCN: web 指相互连接，site 指地点；website 就是由链接搭成的一个地方。

senses.title: An organisation's online home
senses.titleCN: 机构网站：组织在网络上的门面
senses.definition: the online presence of a company, school or public body, where information is published
senses.definitionCN: 公司、学校或公共机构在网络上发布信息的所在
senses.example: Apply through the university website before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 请在截止日期之前通过大学网站申请。
senses.why: A site is a plot of ground; the digital plot is where an organisation keeps its public face.
senses.whyCN: site 本是一块地；数字的「地」就是机构摆放门面的地方。

senses.title: A commercial shop online
senses.titleCN: 网上店铺：可下单选购的站点
senses.definition: a website used for selling goods or services, with pages for browsing and buying
senses.definitionCN: 用于出售商品或服务、可浏览下单的网站
senses.example: Their website takes orders until midnight and ships the next day.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的网站接单到午夜，第二天发货。
senses.why: The site turns into a counter: browsing pages leads to a basket and a payment, and the ground becomes a shop floor.
senses.whyCN: 站点变成了柜台：浏览页面通向购物篮与付款，那块「地」也就成了店面。

senses.title: One address, many pages
senses.titleCN: 一个地址下的整个站点
senses.definition: used of the whole collection of pages under a single domain name
senses.definitionCN: 指单一域名下的全部页面集合
senses.example: The old website is still online, though no one updates it.
senses.exampleCN: 旧网站仍然在线，尽管已经没人更新了。
senses.why: The plural pages are gathered under one name, and that name is the website as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 众多页面被收在一个名字之下，那个名字就是作为整体的网站。

senses.title: As a shortened form
senses.titleCN: 简写：口语中的 site
senses.definition: in everyday speech often shortened to site, especially with a modifier
senses.definitionCN: 口语中常简写为 site，尤与修饰语连用
senses.example: Check the site for the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 去网站上看新的时间表。
senses.why: Speech shortens what print once spelled in two words, and site alone carries the whole meaning in context.
senses.whyCN: 口语把书面曾用两个词写的东西缩短，而 site 单用在语境中已含全部意思。

intro.en: Website is a late twentieth-century compound of web, from Old English, and site, from Latin.
intro.cn: website 是二十世纪后期的复合词，由古英语的 web 与拉丁语的 site 合成。

items.en: Web meant a woven cloth, and later the net of a spider; the sense of connected links came naturally.
items.cn: web 原指织成的布，后指蛛网；由此自然生出「相互链接」之义。

items.en: Situs meant 'a position, a site', from sinere 'to let, to place'; English site came through French.
items.cn: situs 意为「位置、地点」，出自 sinere「放置」；英语 site 经法语而来。

items.en: The World Wide Web was named at CERN around 1989, and web was quickly applied to the linked documents.
items.cn: 万维网约在 1989 年于欧洲核子研究中心命名，web 很快被用在这些相互链接的文档上。

items.en: Website was formed by joining web and site; the exact first printed use is uncertain.
items.cn: website 由 web 与 site 拼接而成，确切首次印行年代不确定。

items.en: The word replaced older phrases such as web site, and site alone now usually means the same thing.
items.cn: 这个词取代了 web site 等较早写法，如今单说 site 通常也指同一事物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers web words that are easily confused with it; the near-meaning group gathers online places and their parts.
note.cn: 形近组收容易与之混淆的 web 类词；近义组收网络场所及其组成部分。

entries.definition: One single page inside a website.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「网页」，是网站中的单独一页。

entries.definition: The network of linked documents, or a spider's net.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「万维网、网」，即互链文档构成的网络或蛛网。

entries.definition: The person who runs and updates a site.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「网站管理员」。

entries.definition: The ability to see, or something seen; not related.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「视力、景象」，与 site 同音但无关。

entries.definition: The short form of website; also any piece of ground.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「网站」（website 的简写），也指任何一块地。

entries.definition: One screen of content within a site.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「页面」，是站点内的一屏内容。

entries.definition: A program on a device, which may replace a website.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「应用」，其功能可以替代网站。

entries.definition: A large site that gathers links and services for users.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门户网站」，集中提供链接与服务。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English web and Latin situs, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 web 与拉丁语 situs，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: web is the linking, site is the place: a website is a place made of links.
normal.cn: web 是连接，site 是地点：website 就是用链接搭起的地方。

normal.en: A webpage is one page; a website is all the pages at once.
normal.cn: webpage 是一页，website 是全部页面加在一起。

normal.en: Every website has an address, just as a site has a location.
normal.cn: 每个网站都有地址，正如一块地有位置。

normal.en: Visit a website is the usual verb; you do not 'look' a website.
normal.cn: 常用动词是 visit；不能说 look a website。

normal.en: The short form site is used freely in speech.
normal.cn: 口语中常直接用简写 site。

abstract.en: Picture many rooms joined by corridors with a sign on every door: the corridors are the web, the rooms are the site.
abstract.cn: 想象许多房间由走廊相连，每扇门上挂着招牌：走廊是 web，房间群是 site。

abstract.en: The word joins an old cloth image to a very old idea of a place, and the result is a place without ground.
abstract.cn: 这个词把古老的布料意象接到同样古老的「地点」观念上，结果是一个没有土地的地点。

abstract.en: One address, many pages: the word is singular because the whole is one place.
abstract.cn: 一个地址，许多页面：这个词用单数，因为整体是一处地方。

examples.en: The school website posts the exam timetable every term.
examples.cn: 学校网站每学期都会发布考试时间表。

examples.en: She built her own website to sell the cloth she weaves.
examples.cn: 她自建网站出售自己织的布。

examples.en: Please check the website for the opening hours.
examples.cn: 开放时间请查看网站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「网（web）下的赛特（site）」——网上搭起的一座赛特城：网站

root: 由现代英语 web（古英语「织网」，万维网）与 site（拉丁语 situs「位置」，经法语）在二十世纪九十年代拼合而成；相关词有 webpage、webmaster。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of website move from a set of linked pages, to an organisation's online home, to a shop, to one whole domain, and finally to the short spoken form.
sensesIntro.cn: website 的五个义项从相互链接的页面，到机构的网络门面，到网店，到整个域名下的站点，最后是口语简写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rooms joined by corridors, a sign on every door.
core.cn: 核心意象：由走廊相连的房间，每扇门上挂着招牌。

branches.en: LINK LINE: pages joined together under one address.
branches.cn: 链接线：同一地址下彼此的页面相连。

branches.en: HOME LINE: an organisation's public face online.
branches.cn: 门面线：机构在网络上的公开门面。

branches.en: SHOP LINE: a site you can buy from.
branches.cn: 店铺线：可以下单购买的站点。

branches.en: SHORT LINE: speech cuts it to site.
branches.cn: 简写线：口语中缩为 site。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a webpage is one room, a website is the building.
branches.cn: 对照线：webpage 是一个房间，website 是整栋楼。

intro.en: Website is a modern compound whose two halves come from very different places.
intro.cn: website 是现代复合词，其两半来自很不一样的地方。

latinIntro.en: Only the second half has a verifiable Latin origin: situs.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后半有可查的拉丁语来源：situs。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 webpage 与 webmaster。

items.example: It forms web-based in related use.

definition_zh: 娶；嫁；与……结婚；使结合、使交融（be wedded to）
definition_en: to marry someone, or to join two things closely together
core_image: 两只手在众人面前交握，从此被一句话绑在一起
scene: 小教堂里只有十几个人，新娘的父亲把她的手交到新郎手里。They were wed in a small church on a rainy April morning.
sceneCN: 这里 wed 是「与……结婚」（第 1 个义项：正式结为夫妻）；句意为他们在四月一个下雨的早晨于小教堂成婚。两只在众人面前交握的手，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：娶、嫁；使成婚；使紧密结合

collocations.zh: 把理论与实践结合起来

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「婚礼」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「已婚的；结合的」
复合词，义为「婚姻状态」，多用于 born out of wedlock
与婚礼相关的同义词根词，义为「新娘的」

senses.title: To marry
senses.titleCN: 结婚：正式结为夫妻
senses.definition: to marry someone, used especially in formal, literary or journalistic writing
senses.definitionCN: 与某人结婚，多用于正式、文学或新闻报道语体
senses.example: The couple were wed last spring in the village church.
senses.exampleCN: 这对新人去年春天在村里的教堂成婚。
senses.why: Old English weddian meant to pledge or to give as a surety; marriage is the chief pledge people make.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 weddian 意为「许诺、作保」，婚姻便是人最主要的一种许诺。

senses.title: To be joined closely
senses.titleCN: 紧密结合：两样东西被牢牢连在一起
senses.definition: of two things, to be joined or combined closely
senses.definitionCN: 指两样事物被紧密连接或结合
senses.example: The old songs wed words to a rhythm that everyone could walk to.
senses.exampleCN: 那些老歌把词与人人能踏上的节奏连在一起。
senses.why: The pledge image works for things too: two sides are bound by a promise-like union.
senses.whyCN: 许诺的意象也适用于事物：两边由一种类似誓约的结合绑在一起。

senses.title: To be devoted to
senses.titleCN: 执着于：一心只守着某观念
senses.definition: in the phrase be wedded to, to be firmly attached to an idea or method and unwilling to change
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be wedded to，指死死守持某种观念或方法而不肯改变
senses.example: The department is wedded to a system that has not worked for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部门死守着一套多年不见效的制度。
senses.why: A vow was meant to be unbreakable, and that stubbornness passes over to opinions.
senses.whyCN: 誓言本意是不可违背的，这种固执便转移到了看法上。

senses.title: Newly married
senses.titleCN: 新婚的：刚成婚的人
senses.definition: used adjectivally in phrases such as newly wed and wedded couple
senses.definitionCN: 以形容词形式用于 newly wed、wedded couple 等短语
senses.example: The newly wed pair left for the coast that same evening.
senses.exampleCN: 新婚夫妇当晚就去了海边。
senses.why: The participle freezes the event into a state, so the marriage becomes a lasting description.
senses.whyCN: 分词把事件凝固成状态，于是这场婚成了持续的描摹。

senses.title: In journalistic headlines
senses.titleCN: 新闻标题中的用法
senses.definition: a short, formal substitute for marry, common in newspapers and announcements
senses.definitionCN: 作为 marry 的简短正式替代词，常见于报纸与公告
senses.example: She wed the lead singer in 1998, a year after the album.
senses.exampleCN: 她在 1998 年与主唱成婚，那是在那张专辑一年之后。
senses.why: Brevity suits headlines, and the word carries just the right formal weight.
senses.whyCN: 标题求短，而这个词恰有合适的正式分量。

intro.en: Wed goes back to an Old English verb for pledging, and marriage was its greatest pledge.
intro.cn: wed 可追溯到古英语表示「许诺」的动词，而婚姻是其中最重的一种许诺。

items.en: Weddian meant 'to pledge, to promise, to give surety', and also 'to marry'.
items.cn: weddian 意为「许诺、担保」，也有「结婚」之义。

items.en: The noun wedd meant a pledge or a surety, the thing given so that a promise would hold.
items.cn: 名词 wedd 意为「誓约、担保」，即为了许诺兑现而交付的东西。

items.en: German Wette 'a bet' and Gothic wadi 'pledge' belong to the same old word group.
items.cn: 德语 Wette「赌注」与哥特语 wadi「抵押」同属这一古老词群。

items.en: Wedded became the usual past form, and wedding came to mean the ceremony itself.
items.cn: wedded 成为常规过去式，wedding 则转指婚礼本身。

items.en: The verb narrowed to formal use, while the metaphor of wedded to an idea kept its force.
items.cn: 这个动词收窄为正式用法，而 wedded to 某观念的比喻仍保有力量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the pledge family; the near-meaning group gathers marriage verbs of different weight.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「许诺」词族的词；近义组收分量不同的婚姻动词。

entries.definition: The ceremony of marriage and the party that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「婚礼」及随之的喜宴。

entries.definition: Married, or firmly attached to something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已婚的」，或「紧密结合的」。

entries.definition: The married state; the -lock element belonged to the old noun pledge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「婚姻状态」，其中 -lock 部分出自古老的「誓约」义。

entries.definition: Pay for work; an old relative of pledge and bet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工资」，与「抵押、许诺」一义有古老亲缘。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for becoming husband or wife.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「结婚」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To marry, often in old texts; also to support a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「娶、嫁」，多见于旧文本，也指拥护某个主张。

entries.definition: To join into one; the plain word for the figurative sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「联合」，是比喻义上的朴素说法。

entries.definition: To end a marriage legally; the opposite act.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「离婚」，是相反的动作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wedd and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wedd，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: wed comes from a word for pledge: a marriage is a promise made public.
normal.cn: wed 出自表示「誓约」的词：婚姻就是一个公开的许诺。

normal.en: Wedding, wedded, wedlock all keep the old vow inside them.
normal.cn: wedding、wedded、wedlock 都把古老的誓约留在里面。

normal.en: Be wedded to an idea means married to it, for better or worse.
normal.cn: be wedded to 某观念意为与它成了婚，无论是好是糟。

normal.en: Newly wed is the headline phrase; the prize is the same as marry.
normal.cn: newly wed 是标题用语，意思与 marry 相同。

normal.en: Past tense wedded is more common than the short wed.
normal.cn: 过去式 wedded 比简短的 wed 更常见。

abstract.en: Picture two hands clasped in front of witnesses: the word is a binding, not just a feeling.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在众人面前交握：这个词是一种约束，而不只是感情。

abstract.en: Anything can be wedded if it is joined by a promise: words to rhythm, theory to practice.
abstract.cn: 只要有约定相连，任何两样东西都能被 wed：词与节奏、理论与实践。

abstract.en: The stubbornness of wedded to is the stubbornness of a vow no one wants to break.
abstract.cn: wedded to 的固执，正是一个谁都不愿违背的誓言的固执。

examples.en: They were wed after ten years of living in different cities.
examples.cn: 在分居两城十年之后，他们结婚了。

examples.en: The design weds old brick to new glass.
examples.cn: 这一设计把老砖与新玻璃结合在一起。

examples.en: He has been wedded to the same routine for decades.
examples.cn: 几十年来他一直执着于同一套常规。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「wed 就是喂（we）到（d）」——一路喂到婚礼上：结婚

root: 古英语 weddian「许诺、担保、婚配」，名词 wedd「誓约、抵押」，与德语 Wette、哥特语 wadi 同源；派生词有 wedding、wedded、wedlock。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of wed grow out of one pledge: marriage, the joining of things, stubborn devotion, the state of being newly married, and the formal word in headlines.
sensesIntro.cn: wed 的五个义项都生自同一个誓约：婚姻、事务的结合、固执的守持、新婚的状态，以及新闻标题里的正式用词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands clasped before witnesses, bound from then on by one word.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在众人面前交握，从此被一句话绑在一起。

branches.en: MARRIAGE LINE: the vow performed, then the state it leaves.
branches.cn: 婚姻线：誓约的践行，以及它留下的状态。

branches.en: JOINING LINE: anything can be bound as if by a promise.
branches.cn: 结合线：任何东西都能像被许诺般绑在一起。

branches.en: STUBBORN LINE: a vow nobody wants to break becomes a habit of mind.
branches.cn: 固执线：无人愿破的誓约变成了思维习惯。

branches.en: STYLE LINE: a short formal verb for newspapers.
branches.cn: 语体线：报纸偏爱的简短正式动词。

branches.en: CONTRAST: marry is everyday, wed is formal and brief.
branches.cn: 对照线：marry 日常，wed 正式而简短。

intro.en: Wed is a native verb from the pledge word; its relatives are all forms of the same vow.
intro.cn: wed 是出自「誓约」一词的本族动词；它的亲属都是同一个誓约的不同形式。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.example: It is the noun behind the verb.

definition_zh: 每周的；一周一次的；名词：周刊；副词：每周一次
definition_en: happening or produced once every week, or a magazine that appears once a week
core_image: 日历上每一排的开头都夹着同一张便签，被反复圈了四圈
scene: 镇上的面包店门口贴着手写告示，每逢周六早上折扣。The shop holds a weekly market on Saturday mornings.
sceneCN: 这里 weekly 是「每周的」（第 1 个义项：每七天发生一次）；句意为这家店每周六早上办集市。日历上七天被圈成一轮，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：每周的；一周一次的
名词：周刊；周报
副词：每周一次地

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根名词，义为「星期；一周」
复合词，义为「工作日」
复合词，义为「周末」
加前缀 bi- 构成，义为「两周一次的」或「每周两次的」，常需说明

senses.title: Happening every week
senses.titleCN: 每周的：每七天发生一次
senses.definition: happening or done once every week
senses.definitionCN: 每七天发生或做一次
senses.example: The team has a weekly meeting on Monday afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每周一下午开周会。
senses.why: The suffix -ly here turns the period into a frequency: week plus -ly means once per week.
senses.whyCN: 此处的后缀 -ly 把时间段变成频率：week 加 -ly 即「每周一次」。

senses.title: Of a weekly amount
senses.titleCN: 按周的：以一周为单位的数量
senses.definition: calculated or paid by the week rather than by the month
senses.definitionCN: 按周而非按月计算的数目
senses.example: Her weekly income barely covers the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周的收入勉强够付房租。
senses.why: The period works as a unit here: the pay packet arrives every seventh day.
senses.whyCN: 这里把周期当单位：薪金每隔七天到手一次。

senses.title: A magazine or paper
senses.titleCN: 周刊：每周出一期的刊物
senses.definition: a newspaper or magazine published once a week
senses.definitionCN: 每周出版一期的报纸或杂志
senses.example: The village weekly prints little more than notices and recipes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份乡村周刊几乎只登通告和菜谱。
senses.why: A publication takes its name from its rhythm, so the adjective becomes a noun.
senses.whyCN: 出版物以其节律为名，于是形容词转成了名词。

senses.title: As an adverb
senses.titleCN: 副词：每周一次地
senses.definition: used as an adverb meaning once a week
senses.definitionCN: 作副词使用，意为「每周一次地」
senses.example: The bins are collected weekly in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天垃圾每周收一次。
senses.why: The same word can answer the question how often without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词形式不变，就能回答「多久一次」的问题。

senses.title: In fixed phrases
senses.titleCN: 固定说法：如 on a weekly basis
senses.definition: in phrases such as on a weekly basis, meaning with a weekly rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 用于 on a weekly basis 等短语，表示按周进行的节律
senses.example: The results are reviewed on a weekly basis, not daily.
senses.exampleCN: 这些结果按周复查，而不是按天。
senses.why: Formal writing dresses the same rhythm in a prepositional phrase.
senses.whyCN: 正式写作把同一种节律装进一个介词短语里。

intro.en: Weekly is a native English formation: the Germanic noun week plus the very common -ly ending.
intro.cn: weekly 是本族英语构词：日耳曼语名词 week 加上极为常见的 -ly 词尾。

items.en: Wicu meant 'a week', with the sense of a turn or a succession of days.
items.cn: wicu 意为「一周」，带有「一轮、一连串日子」的意思。

items.en: German Woche and Dutch week are cognates, and the root may have meant a turn or a change.
items.cn: 德语 Woche 与荷兰语 week 同源，词根原义可能与「轮换、变动」有关。

items.en: The suffix -lic meant 'having the body or form of', and became modern -ly.
items.cn: -lic 后缀意为「具有……的形态」，后来变成现代的 -ly。

items.en: Wekely was used both for 'once a week' and for 'lasting a week'.
items.cn: 中古英语 wekely 既表示「每周一次」，也表示「持续一周」。

items.en: The noun use for a weekly paper or magazine dates from the eighteenth century; the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 指周报、周刊的名词用法始于十八世纪，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other frequency words in -ly; the near-meaning group gathers periods and publications.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 -ly 表频率的词；近义组收周期与刊物类词。

entries.definition: Happening every day; also a daily paper.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「每日的」，也指日报。

entries.definition: Happening once a month; also a monthly magazine.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「每月的」，也指月刊。

entries.definition: Happening once a year; the same -ly frequency ending.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「每年的」，用同样表频率的 -ly。

entries.definition: In a weak way; a near homophone of weekly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「虚弱地」，与 weekly 读音极近。

entries.definition: The period of seven days behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「星期」，是形容词背后的时间段。

entries.definition: A magazine published at regular intervals of any length.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「期刊」，出版间隔可长可短。

entries.definition: Happening every two weeks; the British partner of weekly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「每两周的」，是英式说法中 weekly 的伙伴。

entries.definition: A regular way of doing things, without fixing the period.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「常规」，不固定周期长度。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wicu and -lic, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wicu 与 -lic，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: week plus -ly: the period becomes the frequency.
normal.cn: week 加 -ly：时间段变成了频率。

normal.en: Daily, weekly, monthly, yearly line up in the same family.
normal.cn: daily、weekly、monthly、yearly 排在同一家族里。

normal.en: A weekly is a paper; a daily is a paper too, so the noun works the same way.
normal.cn: weekly 是周刊，daily 是日报，名词化的方式相同。

normal.en: Twice weekly means two times in one week, not two weeks.
normal.cn: twice weekly 指一周两次，不是两周一次。

normal.en: Weakly differs by one letter and means without strength.
normal.cn: weakly 只差一个字母，意为无力地。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with every seventh square circled in the same colour: that repeated circle is weekly.
abstract.cn: 想象一张日历，每隔七格就用同一种颜色圈一次：那一再重画的圈就是 weekly。

abstract.en: The word measures rhythm, not length of time, which is why it works as adjective, noun and adverb.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量的是节律而不是时长，所以能作形容词、名词和副词。

abstract.en: A weekly habit is small but relentless: seven days always come back.
abstract.cn: 每周一次的习惯看似不大却不停歇：七天总会再来。

examples.en: The lab publishes a weekly report on air quality.
examples.cn: 实验室每周发布空气质量报告。

examples.en: He buys a weekly on Fridays and reads it over the weekend.
examples.cn: 他每周五买一份周刊，周末读完。

examples.en: The garden is watered weekly in dry weather.
examples.cn: 干旱时花园每周浇一次水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「围（wee）克（k）里（ly）」——每七天围成一圈，一周一轮：每周的

root: 由古英语 wicu「一周」加后缀 -lic（现代 -ly）构成；同源频率词有 daily、monthly、yearly。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weekly take one period of seven days and use it as a rhythm, an amount, a publication, an adverb, and a fixed phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: weekly 的五个义项把七天这一段当作节律、数额、刊物、副词用法，以及一个固定短语来使用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar with every seventh square circled in the same colour.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上每隔七格被同色圈起的一格。

branches.en: RHYTHM LINE: the same event returns every seventh day.
branches.cn: 节律线：同一件事每七天回来一次。

branches.en: AMOUNT LINE: money counted by the week.
branches.cn: 数额线：以周为单位计算的金额。

branches.en: PAPER LINE: a publication keeps the weekly beat.
branches.cn: 刊物线：一份出版物守着每周的节拍。

branches.en: ADVERB LINE: no preposition needed, the word says how often.
branches.cn: 副词线：无需介词，这个词直接说明频率。

branches.en: PHRASE LINE: on a weekly basis formalises the same rhythm.
branches.cn: 短语线：on a weekly basis 把同一节律说得更正式。

intro.en: Weekly is a Germanic noun plus a Germanic suffix, with no Latin ingredient.
intro.cn: weekly 是日耳曼语名词加日耳曼语后缀，不含拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.meaning: of a kind; in that manner

definition_zh: 重量；体重；砝码；分量、重要性；负担
definition_en: how heavy something is, a heavy object used for weighing, or the importance and pressure that something carries
core_image: 秤盘往下一沉，指针稳稳停在一个刻度上
scene: 邮局柜台上的小秤被包裹压得沉下去，指针慢慢摆回中间。The parcel's weight pushed the scale well past one kilogram.
sceneCN: 这里 weight 是「重量」（第 1 个义项：物体有多重）；句意为包裹的重量让秤的读数远远超过一公斤。秤盘下沉、指针停稳，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：重量、体重；砝码；分量、重要性；负担
动词：加重于；使倾斜；权衡

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根动词，义为「称重；重达；权衡」
加后缀 -y 构成，义为「沉重的；重要的」
加后缀 -less 构成，义为「失重的；无重量的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「权重；加权」

senses.title: How heavy a thing is
senses.titleCN: 重量：物体有多重
senses.definition: the amount that something weighs, measured in kilograms or pounds
senses.definitionCN: 某物有多重，以公斤或磅计量
senses.example: The weight of the box made her put it down twice.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子太重，她不得不放下两次。
senses.why: The noun comes from the verb weigh, and both grow from a Germanic root for carrying.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自动词 weigh，两者都源自日耳曼语表示「承载」的词根。

senses.title: A piece of metal for weighing
senses.titleCN: 砝码：称量用的标准重物
senses.definition: a piece of metal of known mass, used with a balance or as a load in exercise
senses.definitionCN: 已知质量的金属块，用于天平称量或作为负重
senses.example: He added a small weight to the other pan.
senses.exampleCN: 他在另一边秤盘上加了一枚小砝码。
senses.why: A known amount of heaviness becomes a physical object you can pick up.
senses.whyCN: 已知的分量变成了可以拿在手里的实物。

senses.title: The body's weight
senses.titleCN: 体重：身体的分量
senses.definition: the heaviness of a person's body, often spoken of as rising or falling
senses.definitionCN: 人体有多重，常以增减来描述
senses.example: He lost weight during the long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的病中他瘦了不少。
senses.why: From the heaviness of any object the noun narrows to the body: body weight is simply how much you press on the scale.
senses.whyCN: 从任何物体的重，这个名词收窄到身体：体重就是你压在秤上的分量。

senses.title: Importance or influence
senses.titleCN: 分量：影响与重要性
senses.definition: the importance, authority or influence that something carries
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所承载的重要性、权威或影响
senses.example: Her words carry weight in the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她的话在委员会里很有分量。
senses.why: The physical image is kept whole: important words are said to carry weight, as if they pressed down on the listener.
senses.whyCN: 物理意象被整体保留：有分量的言语被说成 carry weight，仿佛它们压在听者身上。

senses.title: A burden or pressure
senses.titleCN: 负担：压在身上的沉重感
senses.definition: a heavy load, physical or mental, that presses on someone
senses.definitionCN: 压在身上的沉重负担，可以是身体上的，也可以是心理上的
senses.example: The weight of the debt kept him awake.
senses.exampleCN: 债务的重压让他夜夜难眠。
senses.why: The same downward force becomes an image of worry: what presses on the mind is described as a weight.
senses.whyCN: 同样的向下之力成了忧虑的意象：压在心上的东西被说成 a weight。

intro.en: Weight is the noun of the verb weigh, and both go back to an Old English word for carrying.
intro.cn: weight 是动词 weigh 的名词形式，两者都可追溯到古英语表示「承载」的词。

items.en: Wegan meant 'to carry, to move, to weigh'; weighing was originally lifting a thing to feel it.
items.cn: wegan 意为「搬运、移动、称量」；最初的称重就是把东西提起来感受轻重。

items.en: German wiegen 'to weigh' and Dutch wegen are cognates of the same carrying root.
items.cn: 德语 wiegen 与荷兰语 wegen 是同一「承载」词根的同源词。

items.en: The noun gewiht meant 'weight', literally what has been lifted and measured.
items.cn: 名词 gewiht 意为「重量」，字面就是「被提起并称过的东西」。

items.en: The noun became weight, and the figurative sense of importance appeared early.
items.cn: 该名词演变为 weight，表示「重要性」的比喻义很早就出现了。

items.en: Medicine and sport fixed the body senses, while politics kept the sense of influence.
items.cn: 医学与运动固定了身体方面的用法，政治语境则保留了「影响力」义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the weigh family; the near-meaning group gathers heaviness, importance and burden words.
note.cn: 形近组收 weigh 一族词；近义组收重量、重要性与负担类词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to measure heaviness or think over a choice.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「称重、权衡」，是本名词的词根。

entries.definition: Heavy, or serious and important.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「沉重的」，或「重大的」。

entries.definition: Having no apparent weight, as in orbit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「失重的」，如轨道中的状态。

entries.definition: To stay until something happens; a homophone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「等待」，与 weight 同音。

entries.definition: The amount of matter in a body, fixed while weight can change.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「质量」，指物质多少，而重量可变。

entries.definition: The quality of being heavy; plainer and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「沉重」，更朴素也少技术味。

entries.definition: The state of mattering a lot; the plain word for the figurative sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「重要性」，是比喻义的平实说法。

entries.definition: A load carried, especially one that is hard to bear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「负担」，尤指难以承受的重负。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wegan and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wegan，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: weigh is the verb, weight is the noun: you weigh a parcel to find its weight.
normal.cn: weigh 是动词，weight 是名词：称包裹为了知道它的 weight。

normal.en: Lose weight and gain weight keep the body sense in motion.
normal.cn: lose weight 与 gain weight 让身体义保持动态。

normal.en: Carry weight means be listened to, as a heavy voice is hard to ignore.
normal.cn: carry weight 意为被人重视，因为沉重的声音难以忽略。

normal.en: A weight on a balance is a known heaviness you can hold.
normal.cn: 天平上的砝码就是一份可以拿在手里的已知重量。

normal.en: Wait is a homophone and means to stay; weight means heaviness.
normal.cn: wait 同音，意为停留；weight 意为沉重。

abstract.en: Picture one pan of a scale sinking: weight is whatever pulls the pan down.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一侧的秤盘下沉：重量就是把它往下拉的东西。

abstract.en: The same downward pull becomes influence in a meeting and pressure in a worried mind.
abstract.cn: 同一种下拉之力，在会议上成了影响力，在焦虑的心里成了压力。

abstract.en: Everything heavy can be measured, and everything important can be said to carry weight.
abstract.cn: 凡沉的东西都能测量，凡重要的事都能说「有分量」。

examples.en: The doctor recorded the baby's weight each month.
examples.cn: 医生每个月记录婴儿的体重。

examples.en: His opinion carries real weight with the board.
examples.cn: 他的意见在董事会里很有分量。

examples.en: She felt the weight of the decision for weeks.
examples.cn: 那个决定的重压让她好几周都难以轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂（wei）特（ght）」——喂饱了的秤盘特别沉：重量

root: 由古英语动词 wegan「搬、称」派生名词 gewiht「重量」，中古英语作 weight；同族词有 weigh、weighty、weightless。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weight run from the measured heaviness of a parcel, to a metal weight, to the body, to influence, and to the burden that presses on a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: weight 的五个义项从包裹被测出的重量，到金属砝码，到身体，到影响力，再到压在心里的重负。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pan of a scale sinking until the needle settles on a mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平一侧下沉，直到指针停在某个刻度上。

branches.en: MEASURE LINE: parcels and bodies weighed on instruments.
branches.cn: 测量线：包裹与身体在器具上被称量。

branches.en: OBJECT LINE: a known heaviness becomes a metal block.
branches.cn: 实物线：已知的沉重变成一块金属。

branches.en: INFLUENCE LINE: a voice that is hard to ignore.
branches.cn: 影响线：难以忽略的声音。

branches.en: PRESSURE LINE: the same pull felt inside the mind.
branches.cn: 压力线：同一种下拉，在心里被感受到。

branches.en: CONTRAST: mass stays the same, weight can change with gravity.
branches.cn: 对照线：质量不变，重量会随重力改变。

intro.en: Weight is a native noun from the weighing verb, and its derivatives use ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: weight 是出自「称量」动词的本族名词，派生词用普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 焊接；熔接；使紧密结合；名词：焊接处
definition_en: to join pieces of metal by heating their edges until they melt together, or to unite things closely
core_image: 两块铁被高温烧得发白，熔在一起，冷却后成了一道凸起的接缝
scene: 修船厂的工人戴着面罩，蓝白色的火花沿着钢板接缝一路走过去。He welded a patch over the hole in the hull.
sceneCN: 这里 weld 是「焊接」（第 1 个义项：把金属边缘加热熔化后接合）；句意为他用焊补片把船壳的洞焊住。烧白后熔在一起的两块铁，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：焊接、熔接；使紧密结合
名词：焊接；焊缝

collocations.zh: 把一个社区紧密联结起来

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「焊工；焊接设备」
加 -ing 构成，义为「焊接」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可焊接的」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「焊接的；紧密结合的」

senses.title: To join metal by heat
senses.titleCN: 焊接：用高温把金属接合
senses.definition: to join pieces of metal by heating them until their edges melt and fuse
senses.definitionCN: 把金属件加热到边缘熔化、融合而接起来
senses.example: The two steel plates were welded along the seam.
senses.exampleCN: 两块钢板沿着接缝被焊在一起。
senses.why: The older sense of the word was to boil or to well up; heat joining two things grew from that image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词更早的意思是「沸腾、涌起」；以热把两件东西连成一体由此长成。

senses.title: To close a gap
senses.titleCN: 焊封：把裂缝或孔洞补上
senses.definition: to close a crack, hole or opening by welding material across it
senses.definitionCN: 用焊接材料把裂缝、孔洞或开口封住
senses.example: They welded the crack shut before the tank was filled.
senses.exampleCN: 油箱装油之前，他们先把裂缝焊封了。
senses.why: A hole is a place where two edges should meet; welding makes them meet again.
senses.whyCN: 孔洞本是两条边缘本该相接之处；焊接让它们重新接上。

senses.title: To unite things closely
senses.titleCN: 紧密结合：使事物连成一个整体
senses.definition: to join or unite things so that they act as one
senses.definitionCN: 把事物连成一体，使之作为一个整体运作
senses.example: Shared work welded the two teams into one group.
senses.exampleCN: 共同的工作把两个团队熔成了一个。
senses.why: The physical fusing is applied to people and plans: once welded, the parts no longer come apart easily.
senses.whyCN: 把熔接的物理过程用到人和计划上：一旦焊住，各部分便不易分开。

senses.title: The joint itself
senses.titleCN: 焊缝：焊出的接合处
senses.definition: the place or line where two pieces have been welded
senses.definitionCN: 两件东西被焊在一起的部位或线条
senses.example: Inspect the welds along the frame every year.
senses.exampleCN: 每年检查框架上的焊缝。
senses.why: The action freezes into a thing: what was a hot process is now a line you can inspect.
senses.whyCN: 动作凝固成事物：原本炽热的过程，如今成了可以检查的一条线。

senses.title: In technical compound uses
senses.titleCN: 技术复合用法
senses.definition: used in technical terms such as spot weld and weld neck flange
senses.definitionCN: 用于点焊、对焊法兰等技术术语
senses.example: A worker made four spot welds to hold the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 工人打了四个点焊把板子固定住。
senses.why: The trade builds its own fixed names, and weld becomes the second half of them.
senses.whyCN: 这一行当自造固定名称，weld 常居其后半。

intro.en: Weld began as a word for boiling and welling up, and only later became the metalworker's term.
intro.cn: weld 最初表示「沸腾、涌出」，后来才成了金属工的术语。

items.en: Wellan meant 'to boil, to well up', and it is the direct ancestor of the modern word.
items.cn: wellan 意为「沸腾、涌出」，是现代词形的直接祖先。

items.en: The past form and the noun were reinforced by Old Norse vella, which also meant to boil.
items.cn: 它的过去式与名词形式受到古诺尔斯语 vella 的加强，后者同样意为「沸腾」。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the verb was applied to metals heated until they joined, and the meaning shifted.
items.cn: 十六世纪，这个动词被用到加热至连接起来的金属上，词义随之转移。

items.en: Industry made it a craft noun: welder, welding, spot weld.
items.cn: 工业使它成了行当日用词：welder、welding、spot weld。

items.en: The figurative sense, to weld people or ideas together, followed from the physical one.
items.cn: 把人和观念「焊」在一起的比喻义，由物理义引申而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words easily confused with weld; the near-meaning group gathers ways of joining materials.
note.cn: 形近组收容易与 weld 混淆的词；近义组收各种连接材料的方式。

entries.definition: A person or machine that welds.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「焊工」或「焊接设备」。

entries.definition: The act of holding and using a tool or power; from a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「挥动、运用」，出自另一个动词 wield。

entries.definition: An old word for a forested area; unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，古语指林区，与此词来源无关。

entries.definition: To join metal with a filler that melts at low heat; weaker than welding.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「锡焊、软钎焊」，用低熔点填料，强度不如焊接。

entries.definition: To melt together into one; the general term for what welding does.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「熔合」，是表示焊接所做之事的通用词。

entries.definition: To stick things with an adhesive, not by heat.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「用胶粘」，不靠热。

entries.definition: To join firmly, often used of materials and of people.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「粘合、结合」，多用于材料与人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wellan and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wellan，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Weld began as boiling: two edges boil and run into one.
normal.cn: weld 起于沸腾：两条边缘烧到沸腾，于是连成一体。

normal.en: Weld together is the set phrase; the result is a welded joint.
normal.cn: weld together 是固定搭配，结果就是 welded joint「焊接接头」。

normal.en: Spot weld joins small points, not a whole seam.
normal.cn: spot weld 只焊几个点，不是整条缝。

normal.en: A welder wears a mask because the light is fierce.
normal.cn: 焊工戴面罩，因为弧光刺眼。

normal.en: Teams can be welded too: once joined, they act as one.
normal.cn: 团队也能被 weld：一旦接上，就像一个整体运作。

abstract.en: Picture two steel edges turning white, then running together and cooling into one raised seam.
abstract.cn: 想象两条钢边烧得发白，随后融为一体，冷却后留下一道凸起的接缝。

abstract.en: The word is about becoming one piece rather than being held together: that is why it is stronger than glue.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的是变成一整块，而不是被固定在一起：所以它比胶更牢。

abstract.en: Any two things that must never come apart can be described as welded.
abstract.cn: 任何再也不能分开的两样东西，都可以说成 welded。

examples.en: The workers welded the new beam to the old frame.
examples.cn: 工人把新梁焊到旧框架上。

examples.en: Their friendship was welded by a hard winter together.
examples.cn: 一起熬过的那个寒冬把他们的友谊焊得很牢。

examples.en: Check the welds for cracks after the winter.
examples.cn: 冬天过后检查焊缝有没有裂缝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威（weld）尔得」——威尔得师傅一烧一按，两块铁就长在一起：焊接

root: 古英语 wellan「沸腾、涌出」，受古诺尔斯语 vella 影响；十六世纪引申为把金属加热熔接；派生词有 welder、welding、weldable。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weld start with heat joining two metal edges, then closing a gap, then binding people, then the joint itself, and finally its technical compounds.
sensesIntro.cn: weld 的五个义项从热把两条金属边接起开始，继而封住裂口、把人联结起来，再指焊出的接缝，最后是技术复合用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two steel edges glowing white, running together, cooling into one raised seam.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条钢边烧得发白，融为一体，冷却成一道凸起的接缝。

branches.en: HEAT LINE: the arc supplies the heat that lets the edges flow.
branches.cn: 热力线：电弧提供让边缘流动的热。

branches.en: GAP LINE: a crack is closed by filling it with molten metal.
branches.cn: 缺口线：用熔融金属把裂缝填上。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: the fusing is applied to teams and friendships.
branches.cn: 人物线：这种熔合被用到团队与友情上。

branches.en: SEAM LINE: the raised trace left when it cools.
branches.cn: 接缝线：冷却后留下的凸起痕迹。

branches.en: TRADE LINE: the craft adds names like spot weld.
branches.cn: 行业线：这一行当添出 spot weld 之类的名称。

intro.en: Weld is a native verb; its derivatives use the common English endings.
intro.cn: weld 是本族动词，派生词用常见的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 西方的；西部的；（Western）西方国家的；名词：西部片
definition_en: in or from the west, or belonging to Europe and North America
core_image: 太阳落到地图左半边，那边是西，人和风都从那一侧来
scene: 傍晚太阳压在地平线上，整片天烧成橙色。They drove west along the coast road until the light failed.
sceneCN: 这里 west 是「西方、西面」（第 1 个义项：太阳落下的方向）；句意为他们沿滨海公路向西开，直到天光消失。

pos.zh: 形容词：西方的、西部的；西方国家（尤指欧美）的
名词：西部影片、西部小说（常大写 Western）

derivatives.zh: 词根本身，义为「西、西方；西部的」
加 -er 构成，义为「西方人；西方居民」
加最高级后缀构成，义为「最西端的」
加 -ward 构成，义为「向西的」

senses.title: In or from the west
senses.titleCN: 西方的：位于或来自西边的
senses.definition: situated in the west, or coming from the west
senses.definitionCN: 位于西侧，或来自西边的
senses.example: The western half of the island is wetter and greener.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的西半部更潮湿、更青绿。
senses.why: The adjective simply takes the compass word west and adds -ern, as in eastern and southern: it names a position on the compass.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把方位词 west 加上后缀 -ern（如同 eastern、southern），表示罗盘上的位置。

senses.title: Belonging to the West
senses.titleCN: 西方国家的：属于欧美的
senses.definition: belonging to Europe and North America, especially their shared culture and institutions
senses.definitionCN: 属于欧洲与北美，尤指其共同文化与制度
senses.example: She studied western philosophy before turning to Chinese classics.
senses.exampleCN: 她先学西方哲学，后来转向中国典籍。
senses.why: Here the word is capitalised in use and means a civilisation, not a compass point: the West as a cultural region.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词实际常大写，指一种文明而非罗盘方向：作为文化区域的「西方」。

senses.title: Facing west
senses.titleCN: 朝西的：面向西方的
senses.definition: facing towards the west
senses.definitionCN: 面朝西边
senses.example: The western windows catch the last of the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 朝西的窗户能接住最后的阳光。
senses.why: A building or room is described by the side the compass says it faces; the meaning turns from origin to orientation.
senses.whyCN: 建筑物或房间按罗盘所指的朝向描述；词义从「来源」转为「朝向」。

senses.title: The western film
senses.titleCN: 西部片：以美国西部为背景的影片
senses.definition: as a noun, a film or novel about cowboys and settlers in the American West
senses.definitionCN: 名词用法，指以美国西部牛仔与拓荒者为题材的电影或小说
senses.example: He watched an old western on Sunday afternoons.
senses.exampleCN: 他周日下午看一部老西部片。
senses.why: The adjective, used as a noun, names a genre: the stories set in the American West, and the word for the direction became the word for that world.
senses.whyCN: 形容词用作名词就指一种类型：以美国西部为背景的故事，于是表示方向的词成了那个世界的名字。

senses.title: Western as opposed to eastern practice
senses.titleCN: 西式的：与东方做法相对的
senses.definition: used to mark the European or American form of something, as in western medicine
senses.definitionCN: 用于标示某事物欧美式的形态，如 western medicine（西医）
senses.example: The clinic combines western medicine with herbal treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所把西医与草药治疗结合起来。
senses.why: In compounds the word becomes a label of method: it says which tradition a practice comes from, not where it is done.
senses.whyCN: 在复合词中这个词成了方法的标签：它说明某种做法源自哪种传统，而非在哪里做。

intro.en: Western is an Old English adjective formed on west, the direction of sunset, with the -ern ending seen in eastern and southern.
intro.cn: western 是古英语形容词，由表示日落方向的 west 加后缀 -ern 构成，与 eastern、southern 同类。

items.en: Westerne meant 'western, lying to the west', built on west with the adjective ending -erne.
items.cn: 古英语 westerne 意为「西方的、在西边的」，由 west 加形容词词尾 -erne 构成。

items.en: The base west is a Germanic word for the direction of sunset, so the adjective belongs to the oldest layer of the vocabulary.
items.cn: 本词 west 是日耳曼语中表示日落方向的词，因此该形容词属于最古老的词汇层。

items.en: West itself named the direction of the setting sun, a word shared by the Germanic languages.
items.cn: west 本身指日落的方位，是日耳曼诸语言共有的词。

items.en: The spelling became western, and the word was used for winds, shores and parts of a country.
items.cn: 拼写演变为 western，用于西风、西岸以及一国的西半部。

items.en: From the sixteenth century it also named the lands of Europe and America as a group, and later the cowboy film.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，它也用来统称欧美诸国，后来又指牛仔电影。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other compass adjectives and the family of west; the near-meaning group gathers words for the West as a region.
note.cn: 形近组收其他方位形容词与 west 一族词；近义组收表示「西方」这一区域的词。

entries.definition: The matching adjective for the east.
entries.definitionCN: 同类形容词，义为「东方的」。

entries.definition: The matching adjective for the north.
entries.definitionCN: 同类形容词，义为「北方的」。

entries.definition: Towards the west; an adverb, not an adjective of place.
entries.definitionCN: 同根副词，义为「向西」。

entries.definition: A person from the West; the derived noun.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「西方人」。

entries.definition: The direction itself; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「西」，是形容词背后的方位词。

entries.definition: A formal word for western, from Latin for the setting sun.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，义为「西方的」，源自拉丁语「日落」。

entries.definition: Narrower: of Europe only, without America.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，范围更窄，只指欧洲。

entries.definition: Travelling towards the west, said of traffic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「向西行驶的」，多用于交通。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root west and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语词根 west，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: West is where the sun sets; western is the side it sets on.
normal.cn: west 是太阳落下的地方；western 就是日落的那一侧。

normal.en: The -ern ending turns a compass point into an adjective, as in eastern and southern.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ern 把方位词变成形容词，如 eastern、southern。

normal.en: Capitalised, the West means Europe and North America as a culture.
normal.cn: 大写时 the West 指作为文化整体的欧美。

normal.en: A western is a film about the American West.
normal.cn: a western 指一部关于美国西部的电影。

normal.en: Western medicine stands opposite Chinese medicine in the phrase.
normal.cn: western medicine 在说法上与中医相对。

abstract.en: Stand facing the sunset: everything on your left hand is west.
abstract.cn: 面朝日落站着：左手边的一切都是西。

abstract.en: The word moves from a direction to a civilisation without changing shape.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一个方向滑向一种文明，形态却不变。

abstract.en: Every map makes its own centre, so western is always western relative to a chosen standpoint.
abstract.cn: 每张地图都有自己的中心，所以 western 总是相对于某个既定位置而言的西方。

examples.en: Western Australia is the largest state in the country.
examples.cn: 西澳大利亚是这个国家最大的州。

examples.en: The museum has a fine collection of western paintings.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆收藏了不少西方绘画佳作。

examples.en: They spent the evening watching an old western.
examples.cn: 他们整个晚上都在看一部老西部片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪死疼」——往西走的人被风吹得歪得要死要疼：西边的

root: 古英语 west「日落的方向、西」→ westerne「西边的」→ 英语 western；同族词有 west、westerner、westernmost、westward。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of western run from a compass position to a civilisation: lying to the west, belonging to the West, facing west, a cowboy film, and a label for method.
sensesIntro.cn: western 的五个义项从方位走到文明：位于西边、属于欧美、朝西、西部片，以及标示方法的西式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun going down on the left half of the map.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳落到地图左半边。

branches.en: THE POSITION: the western half of a place.
branches.cn: 位置线：一个地方的西半部。

branches.en: THE CIVILISATION: Europe and America as the West.
branches.cn: 文明线：作为「西方」的欧美。

branches.en: THE ORIENTATION: western windows take the last sun.
branches.cn: 朝向线：朝西的窗户接住最后的阳光。

branches.en: THE GENRE: a western is a film of the American West.
branches.cn: 类型线：a western 是美国西部的影片。

branches.en: THE METHOD: western medicine names a tradition.
branches.cn: 方法线：western medicine 指一种传统。

intro.en: Western is a native English adjective; the -ern ending and the -er of westerner do the work.
intro.cn: western 是英语本族形容词；起作用的是后缀 -ern 与 westerner 中的 -er。

latinIntro.en: West is Germanic, not Latin; only the scholarly doublet occidental comes through Latin occidens, the setting sun.
latinIntro.cn: west 属日耳曼语而非拉丁语；只有学究气的同义词 occidental 来自拉丁语 occidens「日落」。

items.example: It is the base noun of the family.
It forms western, as in eastern.
It gives occidental, the Latin-side word for western.
items.exampleCN: 它生出 occidental，即拉丁系的「西方」。

definition_zh: 经受住；抵挡；抵抗；承受住压力、攻击或诱惑
definition_en: to be strong enough not to be damaged, defeated or changed by something
core_image: 狂风撞向岩石，岩石一动不动，风只好绕着走
scene: 台风过境，玻璃窗被吹得嗡嗡作响，却始终没碎。The bridge was built to withstand winds of up to two hundred kilometres an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 withstand 是「经受住、抵挡」（第 1 个义项：强壮到不被破坏或击败）；句意为这座桥按能抵挡每小时两百公里的风速来建造。

pos.zh: 动词：经受住、抵挡、抵抗；承受得住

derivatives.zh: 不规则过去式与过去分词，义为「经受住了」
现在分词，义为「正在抵挡」
第三人称单数形式，义为「（他/它）抵挡得住」
加 -er 构成，较少用，义为「抵御者」

senses.title: To bear a force
senses.titleCN: 经受住：承受住外力而不被破坏
senses.definition: to be strong enough to bear a force without being damaged
senses.definitionCN: 强壮到能承受外力而不受损坏
senses.example: The roof is designed to withstand heavy snow.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶的设计能承受大雪。
senses.why: The word joins with, here meaning against, and stand: to stand against a force is to remain standing under it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 with（此处意为「对着」）与 stand「站立」组成：对着外力仍然站住，就是承受住它。

senses.title: To resist attack
senses.titleCN: 抵挡：抵御进攻
senses.definition: to resist an attack or pressure, especially military or verbal
senses.definitionCN: 抵御攻击或压力，尤指军事或言辞上的
senses.example: The walls withstood the siege for three months.
senses.exampleCN: 城墙在围攻下坚持了三个月。
senses.why: The standing image turns defensive: the one who stands does not fall and does not yield.
senses.whyCN: 「站」的意象转为防御性的：站住的人既不倒，也不退。

senses.title: To survive a test of time
senses.titleCN: 经受住考验：历时长久而不坏
senses.definition: to remain in good condition or in force over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期保持良好状态或仍然有效
senses.example: Few ideas withstand the test of time.
senses.exampleCN: 能经受住时间考验的想法并不多。
senses.why: Time is treated as a force like wind or water: the metaphor of physical resistance is extended to endurance.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当成风与水那样的外力：物理抵抗的比喻延伸为持久。

senses.title: To resist temptation
senses.titleCN: 抵挡诱惑：不被人心所动
senses.definition: to refuse to give in to a desire or an influence
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝向欲望或影响屈服
senses.example: He withstood the temptation to open the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他抵住了拆开那封信的诱惑。
senses.why: Here nothing physical presses: what must be stood against is one's own wish, and the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 此处并无实体在压迫：需要顶住的是自己的意愿，而同一个动词兼管两者。

senses.title: To endure hardship
senses.titleCN: 忍受得住：扛过艰苦
senses.definition: to get through a difficult period without being broken by it
senses.definitionCN: 度过艰难时期而未被击垮
senses.example: The family withstood months of cold and hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 这一家人熬过了数月的寒冷与饥饿。
senses.why: The older sense of standing firm shades into endurance: not just not falling, but keeping on.
senses.whyCN: 「站稳」的旧义滑向「忍受」：不只是不倒，还要继续撑下去。

intro.en: Withstand is an Old English compound of with, here meaning against, and stand: to stand against something.
intro.cn: withstand 是古英语复合词，由 with（此处意为「对着、反对」）与 stand「站」构成：对着某物站住。

items.en: Widstandan meant 'to stand against, to oppose, to resist', with wid- carrying the hostile sense of against.
items.cn: 古英语 widstandan 意为「对着站、反对、抵抗」，其中 wid- 带「对着、敌对」之义。

items.en: The prefix with- once meant against in many verbs, as in withhold and withdraw.
items.cn: 前缀 with- 曾在一大批动词中表示「对抗」，如 withhold、withdraw。

items.en: The verb belongs to an old group of compounds whose first element meant against or away.
items.cn: 这个词属于一组古老的复合词，其第一个成分意为「对着」或「离开」。

items.en: Withstonden kept both the physical sense of bearing a force and the moral sense of resisting.
items.cn: 中古英语 withstonden 同时保留「承受外力」的物理义与「抗拒」的道德义。

items.en: The past form withstood was fixed by analogy with stood, and the verb spread to tests of weather, time and desire.
items.cn: 过去式 withstood 依 stood 类推而定形，动词后来扩展到天气、时间与欲望的考验。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other with- compounds and the stand family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of resisting and enduring.
note.cn: 形近组收其他 with- 复合词与 stand 一族；近义组收表示抵抗与忍耐的动词。

entries.definition: To hold something back; another with- compound.
entries.definitionCN: 同前缀复合词，义为「扣住、不给」。

entries.definition: To draw back or take out; the prefix again means away.
entries.definitionCN: 同前缀复合词，义为「撤退、取出」。

entries.definition: To grasp a meaning; formed with stand but unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 形近词，义为「理解」，也由 stand 构成但来源不同。

entries.definition: The irregular past tense and past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 派生形式，即不规则过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: To push back against something, from Latin; broader and more neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抵抗」，源自拉丁语，范围更广、更中性。

entries.definition: To bear pain or hardship over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受」，强调长时间承受痛苦与艰苦。

entries.definition: To carry or put up with something; the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承受」，最平实的日常用词。

entries.definition: To come through something and still exist.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「幸存」，强调事后仍然存在。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English compound with-stand and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语复合词 with-stand，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Withstand is with in its old sense of against plus stand: to stand against.
normal.cn: withstand 就是取 with 的旧义「对着」加 stand：对着站住。

normal.en: The prefix with- also means against in withhold and withdraw.
normal.cn: 前缀 with- 在 withhold、withdraw 中也表示「对抗」。

normal.en: Withstand the test of time is the most common abstract use.
normal.cn: withstand the test of time 是最常见的抽象用法。

normal.en: The past tense is withstood, built on stood.
normal.cn: 过去式是 withstood，由 stood 类推而来。

normal.en: Buildings and bridges are described as built to withstand storms.
normal.cn: 建筑与桥梁常说 built to withstand storms。

abstract.en: Picture a rock facing a gale: the wind must go around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块迎风的岩石：风只能绕过去。

abstract.en: The word measures strength by what remains after the force has passed.
abstract.cn: 这个词用外力过后剩下什么来衡量强度。

abstract.en: Standing is the whole idea: whatever does not fall has withstood.
abstract.cn: 「站着」就是全部：没有倒下的，就是经受住了。

examples.en: The tower has withstood earthquakes for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座塔经受住了六百年来的地震。

examples.en: These plants can withstand long periods without rain.
examples.cn: 这些植物能耐受长时间无雨。

examples.en: She withstood pressure from every side and kept her decision.
examples.cn: 她顶住了各方的压力，坚持了自己的决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为着站」——为着站住不倒，就得抵住风暴：经受住

root: 古英语 wid「对着、反对」+ standan「站」→ widstandan → 英语 withstand；同族有 withstood、withhold、withdraw。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of withstand all rest on standing against something: a physical force, an attack, the wear of time, a temptation, and a stretch of hardship.
sensesIntro.cn: withstand 的五个义项都建立在「对着站住」上：物理外力、攻击、时间磨损、诱惑，以及一段艰苦。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rock in a gale, unmoved while the wind bends around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：狂风中的岩石，纹丝不动，风只能绕行。

branches.en: THE FORCE: roofs and bridges built to carry snow and wind.
branches.cn: 外力线：为承受雪与风而建的屋顶、桥梁。

branches.en: THE ATTACK: walls that hold against a siege.
branches.cn: 攻击线：围城之下仍不倒的城墙。

branches.en: THE TIME: ideas that withstand the test of time.
branches.cn: 时间线：经受住时间考验的想法。

branches.en: THE DESIRE: the temptation not opened.
branches.cn: 欲望线：抵住而没有拆开的诱惑。

branches.en: THE HARDSHIP: a family that gets through cold and hunger.
branches.cn: 艰苦线：熬过寒冷与饥饿的一家人。

intro.en: Withstand is a native compound: the old prefix with- meaning against plus the strong verb stand.
intro.cn: withstand 是本族复合词：旧前缀 with-（意为「对抗」）加强动词 stand。

latinIntro.en: With- and stand are both Germanic; the Latin words for resisting, resistere and sustinere, are unrelated in form.
latinIntro.cn: with- 与 stand 都属日耳曼语；拉丁语表示抵抗的 resistere、sustinere 在形态上与之无关。

items.example: It carries the hostile sense in withstand and withhold.
items.exampleCN: 它在 withstand、withhold 中带对抗义。

items.example: It is the base verb of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个复合词的本动词。

items.example: It forms the past tense withstood.
It builds resist, the Latin-side near synonym.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 resist，即拉丁系的近义词。

items.example: It builds sustain, a Latin cousin in meaning.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 sustain，是语义上的拉丁表亲。
